name: Soul winning & the gospel
about: Preaching the gospel to every creature.

teachings.title: The rich man is wise in his own conceit
teachings.summary: The rich trust in themselves and resist the gospel, as soul winners find, while the poor seek the truth, though welfare can make them wise in their own conceit too.
teachings.text:
Picking up the chapter study at Proverbs **28:1**0;

*The rich man is wise in his own conceit; but the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out.*

We all know the story of the rich young man and Jesus, where he claimed to Christ himself that he had observed all commandments from his youth, and Jesus told him to sell all his things for the poor, and he went away unsaved.

**Matthew 19:24**
*And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.*

Earlier Proverbs told us some of the reasons this is true. Their riches are their strong tower. They place their trust in things.

But, like the rich young man, they are also wise in their own conceits. He thought he had it all figured out. Those that are well off financially often see themselves, their own wisdom and discernment, as the cause for their success., and their wealth as evidence of their righteousness. A feedback loop that keeps them from even questioning the truth. The rich young man sought to be validated by the "good master," and it didn't occur to him that there is none good but God, that the man Christ Jesus sitting there in front of him was the Lord.

Out soul-winning, you encounter far more pushback to the gospel among the wealthy. Even in a more modest neighborhood, if you find a home with a pool, motorsport vehicles, a boat, sports car, or some other sign of wealth, you're likely to great a scoffer at the door.

But the poor? So many are seeking to know the truth. They have nothing else to cling to. Their lives are in turmoil and their futures uncertain and they just seek to know why, and what they can do to know God.

This is why the current welfare system is so cruel. It provides sustenance and comfort. It artificially created the same condition in them as the wealthy. They become wise in their own conceits. Sadly, this is all too common these days.

There are few that are searching out wisdom. There aren't many in America where poverty hits hard enough to make a person stop counting on things and their own entitled arrogance, and be humbled. Praise God for fields of white, ready to be harvested in some areas.

teachings.title: He that winneth souls is wise
teachings.summary: Sowing righteousness and bearing the fruit of the tree of life is winning souls, the greatest wisdom we can share and treasure laid up in heaven.
teachings.text:
Finally, we are also given instruction in character. That gracious women are honorable, but women without discretion are not. That strong men retain their riches and merciful men do themselves good.

*The wicked worketh a deceitful work: but to him that soweth righteousness shall be a sure reward.* How do we scatter righteousness? Winning souls.

*The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; and he that winneth souls is wise.*

The spiritual application to being one who scattererth, sowing righteousness, winning souls and bearing fruit, not hoarding our corn but blessing others...is again agrarian language as a parable for spreading the gospel. The greatest wisdom and counsel one can share. A blessing to those that receive it, and laying up treasure in Heaven for those that freely give it.

And this is the promise of God for our efforts; *Behold, the righteous shall be recompensed in the earth: much more the wicked and the sinner.*

teachings.title: Isaiah 61, the Christian's mission statement
teachings.summary: The words Jesus read from Isaiah 61 are also every Christian's mission to preach the gospel, before the day of vengeance and the resurrection of the righteous.
teachings.text:
The Lord Jesus read from **Isaiah 61** in the synagogue in Galilee, the scriptures being fulfilled there before them. That the Christ the prophets gave witness to was there before them.

And many asked, "isn't that the carpenter's son?"

I have posted many times before that not only does this proclamation, written in Isaiah, and declared by Jesus, give witness to His ministry and His holy purpose and His wonderful salvation, but also serves as a mission statement for all Christians.

In Him, we are filled with the Spirit. We are anointed Priests of the Lord. We are His Ministers, in Christ.

We are to preach the gospel to the meek, to the poor. To give the good news to the brokenhearted. To preach deliverance to those captive in sin, under the bounds of the law. To bring the lost, who are blind to see, and set them at liberty.

To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.

**John 12:47-48**
*And if any man hear my words, and believe not, I judge him not: for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world. He that rejecteth me, and receiveth not my words, hath one that judgeth him: the word that I have spoken, the same shall judge him in the last day.*

Jesus reading Isaiah, leaves off before "*the day of vengeance of our God*."

He was there, in His ministry to bring salvation. But in the last day, when He judges the world by His word, there shall come the day of vengeance.

And in that day, all found to have received His word, who gave been judged and found righteous by His imputed righteousness, will be raised up. Glorified to all nations. Set as rulers over them. Like trees of righteousness, the planting of the Lord.

This is a promise of the resurrection. A covenant made with all believers. And for all our troubles and shame for His sake, we will be blessed with a double portion. Everlasting joy shall be upon us.

*I will greatly rejoice in the Lord, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with ornaments, and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels.*

We, like the seed that dies, and falls, and is sown, we will spring forth, to His glory and praise. Amen.

teachings.title: Don't be a Jonah
teachings.summary: The Spirit prepares hearts long before we arrive, so believers should not run from the call like Jonah but preach the gospel and lay up treasure in heaven.
teachings.text:
Given the proximity and the back and forth war, and peace and trade, many Assyrians had heard of and seen the works of the God of Israel. Many seeds were sown, and watered for this one man to bring forth this much fruit.

Long before Jonah was called, the Lord had helped create fertile ground in their hearts.

Just as Jonah had no understanding of what God had in store, and ran from the divine appointment the Lord had arranged, we have no idea the place people we meet are in. How much work has been done by the Spirit before us.

**John 16:7-11**
*Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you. And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: Of sin, because they believe not on me; Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more; Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged.*

The Spirit is ploughing the hearts and minds of the world. Reproving them. God's mercy is revealed from Heaven in those of us who have believed. His wrath against the ungodly. By creation itself, that men have no excuse.

But the Spirit works on them too, with the conscience given every man, to reprove sinners.

And so when Jesus says the harvest is plentiful, but the laborers few, he is talking to us.

How often are we Jonahs, running from the calling? He led an entire gentile city of Idolatry to call upon the name of the Lord. The rewards for such works are great in Heaven.

**Matthew 6:19-21**
*Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal: for where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.*

How much gold, silver and precious stones do we leave by the wayside for not responding to the call like Jonah?

**1 Corinthians 3:12-15**
*Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.*

How can they believe if there is no preacher?

**Romans 10:14-15**
*How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!*

teachings.title: The great commission is a command
teachings.summary: Rather than ignoring the warnings, chasing hidden knowledge or hiding away, believers are to assemble together all the more and preach the gospel to every creature before the judgment comes.
teachings.text:
**1 Corinthians 10:11**
*Now all these things happened unto them for examples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.*

When Jesus came to the world as the son of man, it was not as the prophets of old. *For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.*

His mission was to show there is peace and goodwill available with the Father, to preach repentance and salvation, grace and mercy to heal the sinner and gather the lost.

But, even in that, as he neared the cross, Christ preached hard against the sin of the Pharisees and the Jews, their destruction to come for the blood of the prophets, and the blood of Christ that they would shed.

The other prophets that came before Christ preached wrath and destruction, of His coming and salvation, but never a man spoke as He did.

But, most of the prophecy of the wrath of His judgment, Jesus gave warning through John, in Revelation.

Today, many ignore the warnings outright. Some argue endlessly about the details, claiming knowledge and insight about the people and events, ascribing to current political and religious leaders traits of the beast and Babylon, and still more choose to believe the hey will be taken out of the way before Tribulation comes, and so they check out, and miss the point for believers.

We are to preach the same message of salvation, mercy and grace to every creature. To share the gospel far and wide. Not to hunker down in fear, in remote villages, or cabins in the woods. Not to dwell in chat rooms and online platforms seeking "hidden knowledge."

We are to gather together, in real life, even more so as the hour draws nigh;

**Hebrews 10:24-25**
*And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.*

And let us share the good news of salvation in Christ to every creature, now before the judgment comes.

*And he said unto them, Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature.*

The great commission is a command.

*The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.*

teachings.title: The twelve spies a picture of the twelve apostles
teachings.summary: The twelve spies bringing first ripe grapes picture the apostles sent two by two to gather the firstfruits, and soul winners today must be of good courage before the harvest.
teachings.text:
**Mark 6:7-13**
*And he called unto him the twelve, and began to send them forth by two and two; and gave them power over unclean spirits; and commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, save a staff only; no scrip, no bread, no money in their purse: but be shod with sandals; and not put on two coats. And he said unto them, In what place soever ye enter into an house, there abide till ye depart from that place. And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear you, when ye depart thence, shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them. Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city. And they went out, and preached that men should repent. And they cast out many devils, and anointed with oil many that were sick, and healed them.*

I was rereading [Numbers 13](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/12541) and it occurred to me the like picture of sending out the 12 spies to the 12 Apostles.

*And be ye of good courage, and bring of the fruit of the land. Now the time was the time of the firstripe grapes*.

The pairs of Apostles sent out to spy out the land and to return with fruits of the Spring harvest. The first ripe grapes. In the area of Judea, in what are subtropical zones, the grapes set their first fruit in April and May. The Bible compares Christ's first coming as being pictured in the Spring feasts. The fruit being those that repented unto the truth. Like the grapes of Eshcol, so were the lost sheep of Israel, gathered by the Apostles, and later the 72 disciples, and of course those who came to believe on Pentecost.

And the message to the soul winners to be of good courage remains true in this time of gleaning, before the fall harvest, bringing in the sheaves at Christ's return.

The agricultural symbolism of the parables and pictures in the Bible provide us a greater understanding to the spiritual things of God. The nature of the seasons and the sowing and planting and harvesting, existing as a means to teach us His ways. All creation exists to reveal God unto us. Amen

teachings.title: Win souls, don't hide in a bunker
teachings.summary: Christians in the collapsing West should not panic or flee to the hills but, like Jeremiah in Jerusalem, stay in their communities winning souls.
teachings.text:
By the way, this is what every Christian who is in the collapsing West should take to heart. Instead of spiraling in fear and reactionary panic, We should remember the promises of God. That we will be delivered. While we may suffer tribulation even unto death, we shall be delivered.

*And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.*

Jeremiah is facing the assured and imminent destruction of his people. Witnessing a famine overtake the land from drought. He is vexed by the filthy conversation of the wicked everyday. And yet he remains separated unto God. He continues to call others to believe, by the word of God.

Yes, Jeremiah is calling out evil. And yes, he's warning the people that they should turn from their sins. But more importantly he's calling people to be saved by faith. He's winning souls.

As depraved and wicked as America is, and knowing the wrath that is upon our people, that has already begun, being ruled by women and foreigners which is a punishment on nations. Having escalating violence against us as a people. Seeing sexual immorality and degeneracy become normalized and targeting children. As wicked as all of that is, we are still a light unto the world as a righteous remnant of believing Christians. There is no other bastion of believers as large in the world. We are blessed with the freedom to preach the gospel to every creature and the resources to actually get it done.

*The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.*

Instead of prepping for doomsday and hiding our light under a bushel in some mountainous retreat, We should be winning souls. Jeremiah isn't in the wilderness far away from the people, but in Jerusalem, the heart of darkness.

Now, I believe it's important to secure the safety of your family, because as a man that's our job, and knowing how to care for them if SHTF is vital, what's more important is doing the work of the Lord. If the great tribulation came tomorrow ( and it's not, we've got a ways down to go), but if the great tribulation came tomorrow, we wouldn't be heading to the hills eating freeze-dried. MREs, but going into the heart of our community, trying to win souls before the day of judgment.

This is a great encouragement. God has given us something tangible that we can do. And we can join in with other members of our community to ensure our deliverance spiritually even if physically it's too late. And in doing so we might delay that judgment and secure a future for our children.

The world is always going to be going to hell in a hand basket. But we are in the time of the harvest and so we should head out to bring in the sheaves.

teachings.title: Preach the gospel as the nation falls
teachings.summary: Like Jeremiah getting people saved as Judah fell, we must win souls, knowing we will not reach enough to stop the coming wrath.
teachings.text:
We should also mention that you see Jeremiah preaching through this whole ordeal as Israel slips into its eventual captivity, and he is no doubt getting people saved. He has better equipped those who trust in the Lord for what is coming by, reconciling them to the Father through the Son.

And that is what we are compelled to do. It's why we are to spread the gospel and go soul winning. Out among the highways and hedges. Compelling people to come to the Lord. It is why we have the Great Commission.

This world is fallen and the god of this world holds men's hearts sway. And while we should standfast preaching against sin and holding to His word, we should do so understanding that we won't reach everyone or even enough that their oblations will prevent the wrath that is to come. That the land itself wants to spew out people who allow innocent blood to be shed with no recompense from the guilty.

**Genesis 9:5-6**
*And surely your blood of your lives will I require; at the hand of every beast will I require it, and at the hand of man; at the hand of every man's brother will I require the life of man. Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.*

teachings.title: Moses full of excuses
teachings.summary: Like Moses we make excuses not to go and preach, but God promises to be with our mouth, and His anger is kindled against those who refuse.
teachings.text:
God has given Moses assurance of His word, the name by which the people may call upon, the power to do wonders and signs. And Moses says, yeah, but I'm not really an elegant speaker. He has another excuse. Not only an excuse, but a lie.

**Acts 7:22** says of Moses; *And Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds.*

So his claim to not be able to lead due to his being "slow of tongue" is just another excuse not to do the will of God.

But to this, God already has an answer:

*Who hath made man's mouth? or who maketh the dumb, or deaf, or the seeing, or the blind? have not I the Lord? Now therefore go, and I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt say.*

Just as Jesus instructs His disciples to not take heed for what they shall say, that the Holy Ghost will put His words in their mouths, so too promises God to Moses.

And stubborn Moses says; *O my Lord, send, I pray thee, by the hand of him whom thou wilt send.* He tells God to send someone else.

*And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Moses.*

We are all called to do the will of the Father. To believe the gospel of Jesus Christ, first and foremost. But then to follow His commandments that we may be well in this life. That we may be vessels by which His will is done. To go out and give the good news to others, being a light that draws those seeking truth to the right paths. To give the gospel to every creature. To lead those in bondage of sin out of spiritual Egypt and to the promised land, the kingdom of Heaven. And for many of us, for much of our lives, we are like Moses. We have every excuse in the book not to go.

We fear no one will believe us. That we don't have the skills. That we don't have the ability to say the right things. That we aren't capable.

But God has already told us in His word, from the red letters in our Bible, "*Take no thought...lo, I am with you until the end of the world.*" We are promised that we will know what to say, the Holy Spirit bringing all things to remembrance. That some may be hard hearted, but that's ok. Those who hear His voice and know Him will believe. That we have the tools already with us to serve Him. That we have been shaped upon God's potter's wheel to be what vessels He needs us to be to serve His purpose. We just need to stop making excuses and go forth to do His will.

Imagine having the anger of the Lord kindled against you because you're full of excuses?

teachings.title: Sent two by two into the harvest
teachings.summary: The sending of the seventy gives the pattern of evangelism, going two by two trusting God to provide, and we should rejoice most that our names are in the Kingdom.
teachings.text:
Beginning in chapter 10 of Luke we see what may be considered the highpoint of Jesus earthly ministry, in so far as success regarding the evangelism of the Gospel, reaching people throughout the region, the lost sheep of Israel, that they may come to repentance, turning towards God. (Jesus' work on the cross being the greatest single act in all human history, aside)

Having successfully preached and reached multitudes, Jesus recruited the 12 from His disciples, and sent them out, two by two before Him. And now, adding an additional 70 to be sent out winning souls.

Jesus says that while the harvest is great, there are too few laborers to bring it all in. This remains true, especially today.

We note the pattern of evangelism given throughout the new testament, echoing what Jesus taught these envoys of the Gospel. Going forth in pairs (not unlike the animals saved from the flood, going forth from the ark of their salvation to multiply their kind), taking with them no provision other than what they carried on their backs, and the word of God. Preaching that the Kingdom of God is nigh.

At each town on these mission trips, they are instructed to find a house to bless with peace and use as a base of operations, and accept what's given them to eat, the shelter offered, having faith that their needs be filled. That the wages of the laborer be paid by the Lord. He says, don't go begging door to door as they preach, just lodge in the first home that is provided them, taking what they are offered.

But if the city reject them, if they find no habitations, to shake the dust and move on. Jesus openly curses the unreceptive cities, saying that with the acts of healing, the signs and wonders of these apostles shown to Capernaum and Bethsaida, even wicked places like Sodom and Tyre would have repented. Woe be unto those places that turned them away.

And, we are told the 70 returned with great joy, carried away by the power they'd been granted to cast out devils in Jesus' name. *And he said unto them, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.*

Jesus promises then that as they minister for Him they would be protected from the power of the enemy. That by no means would Satan be able to harm them in their work. But Jesus also cautions then to remember it is their salvation that they should rejoice in, their part in the Kingdom of Heaven.

So, with a successful group of missionaries and Apostles, hundreds of disciples and multitudes of those saved by their work, Jesus rejoiced in prayer, thanking His Father for this great success, that what seemed good in God the Father's sight, His will be done.

Similarly, we should be likewise thankful, counting the blessing of our part in the Kingdom above all other earthly blessings. Giving thanks to the Lord when we are given success in our labors for Him. Blessed by these things of God which we see. Lives changed. People healed. The spiritually blind made to see. *The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he that winneth souls is wise.* Amen.

teachings.title: Be wise, win souls
teachings.summary: Every saved person is called to the great commission, and as we grow in the word the call to share the gospel becomes hard to resist, so seek out soul winning churches.
teachings.text:
If it isn't clear from scripture, the great commission, the call to be a laborer for Christ, a servant of the Gospel, bringing the good news of eternal life that we are blessed to have been made aware of, to believe on, to be healed by, to others. To love our neighbors enough to go out among the highways and hedges to call them to salvation.

Jesus had followers. Disciples who not only were saved by their faith, calling upon His name, but also the few who left everything to do His work. Who, being called answered. Who took up their cross daily. Who were willing to go out and preach the salvation of the cross to all men. Apostles, messengers of Christ.

Today we are called to do the same. Most of us don't. But the harvest is great and the laborers few. If we are serious in our walk with Christ, if we seek sanctification and separation as we grow in knowledge and faith, invariably we will come to the understanding of this great calling.

To whom much is given, much is expected.

The calling to share the Gospel becomes a driving force in our lives when we walk in His word, in prayer, in thanksgiving. As the Spirit works in us, helping to remove the thorns of sin from our hearts. As our faith grows. It's hard to resist that call.

There are soul winning churches out there, seeking fellow laborers to minister the Gospel. If you want to really grow as a Christian, seek them out. Be wise. Win souls.

teachings.title: Pray the Lord of the harvest for labourers
teachings.summary: Jesus commands us to pray for labourers in the harvest, so even if we do not go soul winning we must pray for those who do and to become one.
teachings.text:
*The harvest truly is great, but the labourers are few: pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he would send forth labourers into his harvest.*

Jesus tells us to pray that God provides laborers for the harvest. That He provide men and women willing to go forth, to the field as it were, to bring in the bounty that is ready to be picked.

If you aren't in a position to go out yourself, pray that you can be. Work towards it. But pray without ceasing for those who are, and that more may come.

Don't allow your own shortcomings, stumbling blocks and snares, perhaps embarrassment that you don't go soul winning for whatever reason (they aren't good reasons, but I am not judging. My excuses for when I don't do it are just as lame), but at least pray for those that do. Pray that God provides more who are willing to go door knocking and evangelizing. Pray you become one of them.

If Jesus tells us to pray, then pray.

teachings.title: Do we do all we can to heal the spiritually sick
teachings.summary: The sign gifts ceased with completed scripture and modern faith healers are grifters, but the Spirit is upon us to preach the gospel, heal the brokenhearted and free the captive, and most of us hardly try.
teachings.text:
Finishing out chapter 8 of Luke, we have in rapid succession Jesus healing the man containing a legion of spirits, sending them into a herd of swine that drove into the sea, the daughter of Jairus, who Jesus raises from the dead, and a woman with a blood disorder that, by faith only, touched the hem of Jesus' garment and was made whole as He made His way to see Juris's daughter.

Luke being a physician continuously shows us Jesus as healer. While on earth, Jesus takes compassion on those that suffer, and does what He can to ease it, in Jesus's case, the virtue of His holy being given to make the sick whole, the dead walk and the demons be cast out.

But it was His mission to heal the sinners spiritually by the promise of faith. To make us whole, forgiven of sin and reconciled with God.

But in everything, by grace and compassion, a charitable love, Jesus gave all.

We aren't Jesus. We are weak vessels for the new man inside us. We can grow in faith and effectiveness for being used by God, as we are called to be, and amazing things will happen in our lives, but we can't literally raise the dead. We can't heal chronic illness. We can't cast out demons. The gifts of the Holy Ghost were for a sign until the completion of scripture, that a people unfamiliar with the Word could be drawn to the truth of Christ.

But, do we do everything we can, giving all we have in our humble power to heal the sick, to set behind devils, to help the perishing escape death?

There are weird sects calling themselves "apostles" and claiming the powers of the Holy Spirit, speaking "tongues," laying hands in dramatic fashion to "heal." Even using the sweat of their garments to act as "prayer cloth" guaranteed to cure what ails, "with just a small token of a love donation...."

These vipers mimic the acts of the real Apostles, in a clown show grift, spouting gibberish and writhing on the ground as if it were them who were possessed by a demon. Claiming power that's not theirs.

But that's not what I mean.

Do we do everything we can, giving all we have in our humble power to heal the sick, to set behind devils, to help the perishing escape death?

Do we live up to that saying of Christ that sets the tone for His mission in **Luke 4**?

*The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, to preach the acceptable year of the Lord.*

The Spirit of the Lord is upon us. He has anointed us into His holy priesthood, the priesthood of believers given charge that we preach the Gospel to every creature. To the poor of spirit that they be made whole. To heal the brokenhearted by the hope we have in Christ.  To preach deliverance to those captive by sin and the cares of this world, in chains to trying to work their own righteousness by the law, and coming short, perish in despair.

Do we do all in our power to make the blind see? Spiritually, giving them the light that comes from the Lord, magnified in us, showing them the right and straight paths? Preaching the word that faith may come, and open their eyes to the truth?

Do we set at liberty those bruised by their iniquities, freeing them from the yoke of sin? The liberty we share in Christ?

Do we preach the acceptable year of the Lord, the Jubilee. The forgiveness of all debts as we are called home to be His people forever in a Kingdom not made of hands?

Do we do everything in our meager power to show compassion on the spiritually sick that they may be healed?

The best of us fall short.

Most of us don't really even try.

And we see how Jesus, who without sin despite being tempted in all ways like we are, studied the scriptures, committed them to heart as a boy, and in constant prayer, seeking to do God's will, loving others, doing whatever He could. And giving all, that those things be fulfilled in Him.

teachings.title: Ephesus Left Its First Love
teachings.summary: The first love the Ephesian church left was winning souls, and a church that stops preaching the gospel to every creature will have its candlestick removed.
teachings.text:
*Unto the angel of the church of Ephesus write; These things saith he that holdeth the seven stars in his right hand, who walketh in the midst of the seven golden candlesticks;*

Jesus begins using a descriptor of Himself, from the description given by John from His vision in chapter 1. Jesus is holding the angels of the 7 churches in His hand. He is walking in this midst of their candlesticks. His message is to the Ephesians, the church founded 30 odd years before the writing of Revelation, by Paul and the other evangelists. That had fornication in their midst back in Ephesians 1. Jesus goes on to praise their good qualities;

*I know thy works, and thy labour, and thy patience, and how thou canst not bear them which are evil: and thou hast tried them which say they are apostles, and are not, and hast found them liars: And hast borne, and hast patience, and for my name's sake hast laboured, and hast not fainted.*

All good things.

*Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love. Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy candlestick out of his place, except thou repent.*

The Ephesians have left their first love. This is generally accepted as the spreading of the Gospel. They are working and laboring and being persecuted in Christ's name, trying false prophets who crept in unawares and rejecting them. But the first love of any church is the winning of souls to Christ. The joy of our salvation when fresh leads to our telling everyone about the good news. Churches grow from giving the Gospel. But many successful churches plateau and settle in with who they have, and get wrapped up in feasts of charity, laboring in their own community of believers while neglecting this command of Christ to preach the word to every creature. Without that, Jesus says, He will remove their candlestick. The church will die.

*But this thou hast, that thou hatest the deeds of the Nicolaitanes, which I also hate.*

Another compliment, that the church at Ephesus hates the deeds of the Nicolaitanes. We have to discern from this limited information that they were a group either led by or claiming to be followers of someone named Nicolas. Many speculate that it refers to Nicolas the proselyte from Antioch, who was elevated to decon along with Stephen and Philip back in Acts.

The doctrines refered to here, according to early writings and histories is that Nicolas, a pagan convert to the faith of the Jews, then accepting Jesus as the promised Christ, had the doctrine of despising the flesh, hating the material world, that he could better focus on the spiritual. The idea is given he was a just believer, but those who came after him took his views and drifted heavily into gnosticism. We can't know directly from scripture, but this seems very likely. It's also possible that gnostics took the name as a way of gaining legitimacy in the early churches, that they may creep in unawares, with damnable heresy.

*He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of God.*

The first promise to those who overcome, who believe on the Lord Jesus Christ for salvation, is the gift of eternal life. The eating of the fruit of the tree of life, in the midst of the paradise of God. The location is going to come up later in Revelation, but the important thing is the knowledge that we who believe in He that has overcome will be given of it to eat.

Recall in Genesis 3 that God banishes Adam and Eve from the Garden to prevent their eating of this tree themselves, having already eaten of the tree of knowledge of good and evil. Having sinned.

teachings.title: The seed groweth, he knoweth not how
teachings.summary: The kingdom grows like sown seed and a mustard tree, God not dictating which seed sprouts, a rebuke of Calvinism and a picture of believers branching out by leading others to Christ.
teachings.text:
*So is the kingdom of God.*

Jesus uses all these things of His own creation to make simple the ways of God to us.

And a man sows seed, which grows after its kind, blade, and ear and fruit. He doesn't make it grow, it just does, and when it is ripe for the harvest he brings in the bounty.

And so is the Kingdom of Heaven. The seed is the word, Jesus tells us, and it will *spring and grow up, he knoweth not how.* Meaning God, represented as the farmer doesn't dictate to the seed that it germinate, that it sprout, when it should flower and bud, that it bear fruit. Only that it will as it will, and in due season be ready for harvest.

Obviously God knows *how,* but the point is He doesn't determine which seed sprouts, or the nature of how it grows.

It's a rebuke of Calvinism, but it is meant to give us understanding of the Kingdom and our role in it. Both as the sowers and the sheaves. How Heaven grows.

*And he said, Whereunto shall we liken the kingdom of God? or with what comparison shall we compare it?*

We are privy to these lessons. We are not given the parable only, for those with ears to hear, but given their meaning. Nothing hid. And scripture gives us the meaning that we who believe may gain deeper understanding.

Heaven is like a mustard seed, tiny but that grows massive trees, with branches spanning out, each branching further. We are the branches sprung out from the seed. We can trace our lineage in terms of believers who led others to Christ, who led still others, who eventually were those who brought us to salvation. Like a family tree, stretching back to the seed that was sown.

 *For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ. For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body, whether we be Jews or Gentiles, whether we be bond or free; and have been all made to drink into one Spirit.*
*For the body is not one member, but many.* **(1 Corinthians 12)**

The Kingdom of Heaven is *like* this. And for our understanding all of creation exists.

*And with many such parables spake he the word unto them, as they were able to hear it.*
*But without a parable spake he not unto them: and when they were alone, he expounded all things to his disciples.*

teachings.title: Go to the highways and bid all to the feast
teachings.summary: As God's servants our role is to go out to the highways and compel all, bad and good, to come to the wedding feast of the Son.
teachings.text:
Make no mistake, as servants of God, this is our role.

We are the sons who do labor in the field for the harvest. We are the loyal husbandmen, tending the Lord's vineyard, and bringing to Him the fruit of the harvest. We are the servants bidding all to come to the wedding feast of the Son.

We are commanded to win souls to Christ. To go out along the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage. Both bad and good. That they may attend in the raiment fit for a wedding feast.

**Revelation 3:5**

“*He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.”*

Our role as those obedient to the Gospel is to go out to give the same Gospel that saved us to every creature, and compel them to come in, that God's house may be filled.

teachings.title: Fruit of souls won, and false prophets who bear none
teachings.summary: Throughout the New Testament the work of believers is winning souls for God's increase, while false prophets with doctrines of works and philosophy cannot bring forth that fruit.
teachings.text:
Paul continues his greeting to the churches in Colosse, including a shout out to the early church in Laodicea, churches he himself didn't establish in person, as the Gospel has been preached throughout the world, faith to faith, to the Gentiles, beyond even Paul's direct ministry.

All believers, members of the body of which Jesus is the head, united in spirit, in the joy of peace with God through grace and faith, sharing the goal of bringing increase, the harvest of fruit of righteousness, winning souls to Christ with the Gospel of reconciliation. Bringing forth fruit meet for repentance. Turning those that heard and believe towards God.

We see in epistle after epistle, in the Acts of the apostles, in Jesus' own ministry, and His sending of disciples out, two by two into the highways and hedges. We see it in John the Baptist's preaching in the wilderness. It is faith shared and souls won. To God the increase.

The so called holy men, vipers chastised by John and Jesus Himself, Peter and Paul, were unable to bring forth this fruit, to lead believers to Christ.

Neither can false prophets, and yet they are here in Colosse as they were in Galatia, Ephesus, in the Judean wilderness, as Satan himself, trying to lead the churches astray, causing others to sin, and damning souls with their doctrines of works.

It's the same play as Satan in the desert with Christ. We see it today. They beguile us with enticing words, to *spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ.*

teachings.title: Ambassadors of reconciliation
teachings.summary: Our letters of commendation are the souls we win, our glorified body is sure but clothed by our works, and as new men reconciled to God we are ambassadors bringing others the same reconciliation.
teachings.text:
Continuing the theme of the previous chapters, which of you recall, started regarding letters of commendation among men. Paul reminds that our letters of commendation are those who have believed because of our sharing the gospel. He says we are being judged by the conscience of the unbelieving, that our behavior should reflect the light that's within us, living as a light that guides them through the darkness put over them by the devil, winning them to Christ.  That we are ministers of the same Gospel of mercy that changed our hearts and brought us to focus on the things unseen, our conscience clear in Jesus.

Building on this, Paul writes about our physical bodies perishing, but our glorified body from Heaven assured. That the Holy Spirit within us is the earnest, the down payment from God on His promise. But our eternal body is naked, being new born. It is clothed and housed in raiment earned by our works here, judged by God, and so we should constantly strive in this body for that which we will receive in the next.

Preferring being absent this body to be present with the Lord, we should live without fear. What are we threatened with? Heaven? As Jesus said "In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you." We should live with the confidence that this is true and that we are furnishing the mansion He has provided us, winning souls to Christ.

By focusing on the unseen, living the faith, we also give answer to those that judge by appearance rather than of the heart, as God judges. And in doing so, be able to pierce the veil of darkness and bring them to the light of God reflected in us.

We are a new man, contained in the earthen vessels of the old, but reconciled with God in Jesus, and so, given the ministry, being a servant, to spreading that reconciliation to others. Ambassadors.

Paul says it better than I can, go read the first 5 chapters again.

teachings.title: Peter sent to Cornelius
teachings.summary: As with the eunuch and Saul, God sent a man to preach to Cornelius, and God being no respecter of persons in the gospel does not undo His hierarchies or the nations and borders He sets.
teachings.text:
Now we find in Acts 10 the story of Cornelius, a Roman centurion stationed in Samaria, in the port city of Caesarea and someone who was devout to God, but not saved. Praying and giving alms, God-fearing and fasting, but in ignorance of the truth of the gospel. And God, seeing his searching for truth sends him a vision of an angel telling him to send men to bring Peter to him, that "*he shall tell thee what thou oughtest do.*"Just as the Lord tells Saul in chapter 9 to wait on Ananias.

And, similarly to Philip in chapter 8 with the Ethiopian eunuch and Ananias to Saul in 9, we see God telling Peter to go unto Cornelius.

This is important. Things God repeats we should pay attention to. The angels and visions and even the glorified appearance of Jesus, none give the gospel but rather send saved men to preach the word and get other men saved. We are called to be ministers of reconciliation, that we may save some. Don't miss this point, for it applies as much today as it did here. It is by man acting as agents for God, a royal priesthood sharing the Gospel, that by hearing man may come to believe.

Peter is in Joppa, and sees a vision from God showing every type of animal, clean and unclean according to Masoretic law, and God tells him to slay and eat. Peter, that stone, protests saying he has never eaten an unclean thing. God, using this illustration to show Peter he must preach to the Gentiles, says nothing is unclean if God has cleansed it.

This is an allegory for preaching to the Gentiles, but it also serves as a reminder that the carnal ordinances and dietary laws that were a picture of the better Testament to come are done away with in Christ. That no meat is unlawful for a saved Christian to eat, that is blessed by God.

It's interesting that the vision is repeated to Peter 3 times before he wakes from it. Just as Peter denied Christ 3 times and as he was instructed by the risen Jesus 3 times to feed His sheep. God repeats things he wants us to understand, and Peter is no different than us in his being slow on the uptake sometimes.

The messengers sent by Cornelius arrive as Peter comes out of his vision, and understanding through the Spirit that he is to go with them,

Cornelius, who anticipating Peter's arrival has gathered not just his household, but his kinsmen and close friends, falls to Peter's feet and worships him, but is rebuked by the Apostle. "I am just a man."

Peter, now in a household full of Gentiles, who being in Palestine and living among Jews, mentions to the gathered that under Jewish custom he was forbidden from doing what he is doing, but that God's vision had shown him differently.

Peter says he understands now that God is not a respecter of persons.

Neither should we be when it comes to the Gospel, and serving our brothers in Christ. There are no men of any race or ethnicity to whom we should think they are unclean in the spirit of giving the Gospel. This isn't as universalist as it is portrayed. We should treat every human being as we would have them treat us, and in matters of God, rich or poor, bond or free, Jew or Greek, man or woman, all the same in Christ.

This does not however do away with our hating the wicked who hate God, the hierarchy of rule given by God for the powers that be; child to mother to husband to God, congregants to deacons to pastors to Christ, paying custom and tribute to those who rule, with God above all. And the establishment of nations and borders, which are drawn and redrawn by God to His purpose. This is not being a respecter of persons but rather respecting God and His Judgement. Too few understand this and in their ignorance and pride, err one way or the other in this, following their own judgement instead.

teachings.title: Ananias sent to Saul
teachings.summary: Jesus appeared to Saul but sent a man, Ananias, to give him the gospel, showing that people are saved by hearing the word from saved Christians, a duty too many shirk.
teachings.text:
Acts 9 tells the story of Saul/Paul's 'seeing the light' on the road to Damascus. He had gone from a student of the Pharisees taught by the high priest Gamaliel, to a participant in the martyrdom of Stephen, to becoming a zealous persecutor of the church in Jerusalem, to the point where the disciples were scattered abroad.

Now, seeking to further put down what he saw as a blasphemous uprising, he asked permission to go and arrest Jews in another nation, Syria. With that license, he set off on the journey only to be struck blind by the appearance unto him of Jesus Himself.

Saul, astonished and fearful responds to Jesus' rebuke, asking "Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?"

And, Saul blindly asks "Who art thou Lord?" Jesus identifies Himself, and repeats the charge against Saul of persecuting Him, through His church.

Jesus tells him it is "hard for thee to kick against the pricks." A idiom of the time, referring to the pricked stick used to steer an ox in the field. It means that the more you fight it, the harder it's going to be, as an ox who kicked against the prick would only further imbed the sharp ends. (Modern versions omit this verse because they are written by reprobates who take away from the word of God).

Blinded and desperate, Paul asks what he must do, and Jesus directs him to Damascus, where he will be told. In Damascus, a disciple Ananias is given a vision by the Lord to go to Saul, and give him the truth of the Gospel, laying hands on him that he might be gifted by the Holy Ghost to be a great man of God, preaching to kings and spreading the Gospel to the Gentiles.

Naturally, Ananias protests. This is Saul who has been breathing threats and slaughter against believers. Who had a warrant to arrest them in the city. Now Jesus was asking him to go, in faith and visit him, that he might see.

Three days without sight, fasting, without drink, Saul was praying to God for answers, visited with a vision of Ananias coming and healing him.

Here we see that while Jesus appeared and struck Saul blind, He doesn't give Saul the answer to what he must do, but rather a man must go to him and bring him to Christ.

We are called upon by God to bring people the truth. It is from faith to faith, by hearing the word of God from saved Christians, that brings them to salvation. Jesus could have told Paul in that vision, but that's not how it works. We are the laborers who sow, water and harvest. It is an awesome responsibility. One too many of us shirk, under far less threat and danger than Ananias here.

He was called to go into the den of those who sought to arrest or kill him, on faith he obeys and brings perhaps the most influential Christian in history, to the Lord. If he can do that, we can give the Gospel to a coworker, friend or neighbor, with only the threat of being mocked or rejected standing in our way.

So, it is with that understanding and faith that Ananias goes to his enemy, and heals him, and Saul, now Paul, able to see, believes and is baptized in Jesus' name.

Paul himself tells the story again in Acts 22, with a bit more detail, which we will see. But his conversion, seeing the light, being once blind but now seeing, becomes the chief analogy for Christians being born again.

teachings.title: I am the vine, ye are the branches
teachings.summary: The fruit of John 15 is souls won, and a fruitless believer is set aside from usefulness, not cast into hell, for the passage speaks to the saved about service.
teachings.text:
A slight continuation of John chapter 14, Jesus is giving His saved followers final instructions, calling on them to win souls for God. The fruit they bear are converted and saved Christians, who like a branch of a vine then produce more fruit, and so on. Branching out and on, one long vine back to Him, the true vine.

God the Father being the husbandman, the planter of the vine, the one who receives the fruit.

We are called as Christians to be *meet for the master's use, and prepared unto every good work.* To live in the word, reading scripture, in prayer, sanctified, abiding in Christ so that we may be able to bring forth that fruit.

If we don't, if we stay carnal, stay in the flesh, not living in Christ but instead the world, we become useless. Withered and dead, producing no fruit. And God "fires" us.

Some take this verse out of context to say that we can lose our salvation and that we are cast to Hell, but every mention of fire isn't about Hell. Rightly dividing the word of God often comes down to knowing if it's being addressed to saved or unsaved, about salvation or about another topic. This is one of those cases.

We should glorify the Father by being soul winning examples, bearing much fruit. Being Christ's disciples. Not all saved believers rise to this. In fact few do.

These are the commandments mentioned in v10, the preceding 9 verses. Not the 10 commandments, but being worthy Christians bearing fruit. It's specific context to the chapter.

teachings.title: One soweth and another reapeth
teachings.summary: Jesus' meat was winning souls; some sow, some water and some reap, and all rejoice together over the souls won.
teachings.text:
Now His disciples who had returned with food try to get Jesus to eat, but he takes the opportunity to explain His meat is doing His Father's work; winning souls.

As is often the case, Jesus explains by comparing their sharing the faith with harvesting. He points to the gathering Samaritans that they are ripe to be harvested.

He tells the disciples that their labors in gathering will be rewarded, even as the sower will be. In our labors for Christ, some of us will sow seeds and never see if they germinate and grow to fruit ripe for harvesting. Some of us water the seeds sown by others. Some are blessed to reap. All will rejoice in Heaven when we meet those we've helped win to the Lord.

Jesus preached for 2 days and they believed on Him, having seen for themselves that the report of the woman was true.

teachings.title: Call upon me in the day of trouble
teachings.summary: God's call to call upon Him in trouble is the gospel to all men, and believers let their light shine so men glorify God.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 23:23**
*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone*.

These aren't the repetitive acts done by priests, but matters of the heart which God judges, and that He seeks from us.

Having established His ways, God continues in v15 to give the Gospel message. The good news to all men in all ages; the dispensation of grace:

*And call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me.*

Calling upon the name of the Lord for salvation, that we may glorify Him to all men. The promise of salvation and the heart of the great commission, coupled with the truth that we magnify His light, when we are in Him, that man may see our works of righteousness, mercy and thanksgiving, and glorify God.

**Matthew 5:16**
*Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.*

This is our purpose as believers. To give the judgment of God and an example of His mercy, praising His name in thanksgiving, all as an outlet to be seen by man, that He may be glorified.

teachings.title: Have you ever cried out to the Lord for help
teachings.summary: Nearly everyone has cried out to God for help, which opens the way to show them they must call upon the Lord to be saved.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 12** opens with the most plaintive cry, yet. Calling upon the Lord, "Help."

That simple prayer, asking for help during our trials, is perhaps the most often prayed.

"Help, Lord" because the circumstances have led to humble ourselves before Him. Our admission of weakness allows God to be our strength, and glorifies Him that deserves all glory.

Even the erstwhile atheist, the fool who says in their heart, "there is no God," cries out for help from the deity they profess doesn't exist.

We often will ask someone we give the gospel to, have you ever called out to the Lord for help? Because of health, or the health of another. Cry out in fear, because of a crisis or an emergency need has left them no other way to turn, except towards the Lord and His mercy. Or something as simple as a job, or test. Nearly all will say "Yes" if they're being honest.

From there, it becomes easier to lead them to the truth that they need to call upon the name of the Lord specifically to save them, eternally. To receive forgiveness of sin and everlasting life.

If man struggles with the things of this world on his own, how much more do we need help for the spiritual things of God?

Have you cried out to the Lord? Have you come before God, unable to go on, let alone articulate the need you are petitioning, beyond a simple "Help?"

Have you called upon the Lord for salvation?

teachings.title: When they say they are a good person
teachings.summary: When soul winning, those who deny they sin can be shown Revelation 21:8 on all liars and Proverbs 24:9 that even the thought of foolishness is sin, while scorners are left behind.
teachings.text:
While it is rare, there are times when you are out soul-winning, or giving the gospel to others, where the person refuses to admit that they sin. Recognizing one has fallen short of the glory of God is a key step on the Roman's Road. Sometimes, it's pride, other times it is ignorance, but regardless of the source, some people just think they are "a good person."

Most experienced soulwinners will turn to Revelation 21:8;

*But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death.* Here, we would highlight "all liars," and make the sincere appeal, "We have all told lies." This will often break the impasse. It is difficult to say to anyone with a straight face that you do not and never have told a lie.

But for some who can't admit to being a liar, I have found **Proverbs 24:9** works well to push past that, because while we might justify our dishonesty to others as "harmless," or a "little white lie," everyone has stray thoughts and intrusive ideas that we are ashamed of. Covetous, lustful, wrathful and ultimately foolish.

Some will pushback to any gospel presentation with scorn, those are an abomination. We shake the dust and move on.

teachings.title: Wisdom's feast and the gospel invitation
teachings.summary: Wisdom's feast pictures the gospel invitation in which Christ the bread of life calls all, simple and wise, good and bad, to come and freely take the water of life.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 9** concludes the preface of Proverbs, the instruction of Solomon to his son on Lady Wisdom and the strange woman of folly.

Wisdom's table is set for the feast, her house ready, her wine mingled (the restoration of the preserved fruit of the vine mixed with water, spiced with myrrh, sweetened with honey), her maids sent to call all who would enter in to come.

*Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither: as for him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him, Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine which I have mingled.*

The unadulterated truth of God's word is that wine. The bread which has come down from heaven is Jesus.

**John 6:32-36**
*Then Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Moses gave you not that bread from heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven. For the bread of God is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world. Then said they unto him, Lord, evermore give us this bread. And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst. But I said unto you, That ye also have seen me, and believe not.*

Her maidens calling out to the feast of Wisdom as the parable of the wedding feast:

**Luke 14:16-23**
*Then said he unto him, A certain man made a great supper, and bade many: and sent his servant at supper time to say to them that were bidden, Come; for all things are now ready. And they all with one consent began to make excuse. The first said unto him, I have bought a piece of ground, and I must needs go and see it: I pray thee have me excused. And another said, I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to prove them: I pray thee have me excused. And another said, I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come. So that servant came, and shewed his lord these things. Then the master of the house being angry said to his servant, Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor, and the maimed, and the halt, and the blind. And the servant said, Lord, it is done as thou hast commanded, and yet there is room. And the lord said unto the servant, Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled*.

Just as both the simple and the wise are compelled to turn hither to Wisdom's feast, so too the gospel is for both good and bad;

So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests.

**Matthew 22:10**
*So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests.*

Jesus crying out in the streets, telling all to come to Him;

**John 7:37-38**
*In the last day, that great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink. He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.*

Forsake the foolish and live! Whosoever will, let him come.

**Revelation 22:17**
*And the Spirit and the bride say, Come. And let him that heareth say, Come. And let him that is athirst come. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely*.

The invitation of God to wisdom, to knowledge and understanding, is the invitation to life; as a wedding feast laid out by the host. Where the wise enters into the meal already prepared. The wine mingled. The wedding clothes, laid out, white and pure. To eat that bread of life and drink that living water, never to hunger or thirst again.

teachings.title: Bidding all to the Passover feast
teachings.summary: Hezekiah's call to all Israel to the Passover, a picture of Christ, is like the king's wedding parable where many made excuses but bad and good were compelled to come and were pardoned.
teachings.text:
The revival led by King Hezekiah continues, and he leads the great restoration of the Passover, the feast of unleavened bread, which is given to Israel as a picture of Christ.

The King bidding all Israel to the feast of the lamb slain for their iniquity is similar to this parable told by Jesus in **Matthew 22:1-10**

*And Jesus answered and spake unto them again by parables, and said, The kingdom of heaven is like unto a certain king, which made a marriage for his son, And sent forth his servants to call them that were bidden to the wedding: and they would not come. Again, he sent forth other servants, saying, Tell them which are bidden, Behold, I have prepared my dinner: my oxen and my fatlings are killed, and all things are ready: come unto the marriage. But they made light of it, and went their ways, one to his farm, another to his merchandise: And the remnant took his servants, and entreated them spitefully, and slew them. But when the king heard thereof, he was wroth: and he sent forth his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned up their city. Then saith he to his servants, The wedding is ready, but they which were bidden were not worthy. Go ye therefore into the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage. So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests.*

Just as with Hezekiah's letters to all Israel, many made excuses, or mocked the invitation. But many were compelled to come, turning their heart to the Lord.

And as Jesus' parable, both bad and good came. People who were ceremonially unclean, yet sought after the Lord God of Israel. And Hezekiah begs their pardon of the Lord, and our merciful God grants it, a picture of the fact that while we were yet sinners Christ died for us.

teachings.title: Revival forces men to choose life or death
teachings.summary: Preaching and soul winning force people to choose life or death; some are saved, many harden themselves, and our job is to work the harvest and force the issue.
teachings.text:
The nature of revival, of proclaiming the truth of God to all men, to soul-winning and contending for the faith, and challenging false ways and compromise, is that it forces people to choose.

We often talk of God's constant winnowing, the separation of the wheat from the chaff, which is shown throughout the Bible, but the truth is, God is constantly giving men a choice. He is offering us the truth and life, and placing the choice on our hearts.

**Deuteronomy 30:15-20**
*See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil; In that I command thee this day to love the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply: and the Lord thy God shall bless thee in the land whither thou goest to possess it. But if thine heart turn away, so that thou wilt not hear, but shalt be drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them. I denounce unto you this day, that ye shall surely perish, and that ye shall not prolong your days upon the land, whither thou passest over Jordan to go to possess it. I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live: That thou mayest love the Lord thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days: that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.*

**Joshua 24:15**
*And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.*

Forcing people to make this choice is the purpose of revival. It is the fruit of preaching the word and going out to win souls. It forces people to choose.

Some will hear the word and be converted unto eternal life. But many will reject Christ and decide to harden their hearts and hold the truth in unrighteousness.

The revival led by King Josiah was shortlived. When he died in battle, his sons were made king, first Jehoahaz, who was then carried away to Egypt, and then Eliakim aka Jehoiakim. Both did evil in the sight of the Lord. In our study of **Jeremiah**, we covered these kings and the wickedness of Judah in their day, when Babylon came and made Jerusalem a desolation, fulfilling the word of God. They did evil in the sight of the Lord and willfully and knowingly turned to the sins of their fathers and the abominations that they did.

The Lord giving Judah one last chance to know the truth, to have it read to them by Josiah, and acted upon by his hand, meant that while many believed unto righteousness, most chose death.

So that when God's wrath came upon them, they were without excuse.

Soul-winning is what we are called to do, but the more we do it, the more the gospel is proclaimed to every creature, and gone out to all the world, the more people will become reprobate. Even our own families.

At some point, the fullness of the Gentiles will come in. Everyone who will be saved will be, and the rest will choose to worship the beast and take his mark, and condemn themselves.

Our job is to go work the harvest. To force the issue. To make people decide if they choose life or death.

teachings.title: Not peace but division: pressing loved ones to decide
teachings.summary: Christians hesitate to press loved ones to decide for Christ for fear of losing them, but loving family more than Christ makes us unworthy of Him.
teachings.text:
**Luke 12:51-53**
*Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division: For from henceforth there shall be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three. The father shall be divided against the son, and the son against the father; the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother; the mother in law against her daughter in law, and the daughter in law against her mother in law.*

This idea of division is confusing for some, but it is something that I think saved Christians understand by the Spirit, even if they don't intellectually.

We all have had loved ones, family, friends, who we have shared the gospel with and given the good news to, but we hesitate to push the issue. To bring them to make a decision. To force them to either accept or reject the truth that's saved us. The grace that we stand on.

Sometimes, it's embarrassment at our own sins being evident to those who know us best. Fear of being exposed as a hypocrite.

But often, it is the understanding that pushing the issue may push them away. That in trying to save them, we could lose them. And that nagging feeling that if we do, we lose them forever and that they will condemn themselves.

Christians are often so afraid that our loved ones will perish and be damned, but at the same time are scared we could be the cause of it. We love them more than the truth of Christ and our indecision and fear of making them choose comes from that. And the spiritual discernment to know it may be their final decision, reprobating themselves.

**Matthew 10:37**
*He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me: and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.*

teachings.title: How long halt ye between two opinions
teachings.summary: Most people avoid deciding, but preaching the gospel forces them to choose eternal life in Christ or rejecting God and being given over to a reprobate mind.
teachings.text:
The great story of Elijah vs the prophets of Baalim, even the prophets of the groves who ate at Queen Jezebel's table.

God sends Elijah back to the Northern Kingdom of Israel after 3 and a half years of drought and famine.

**Luke 4:25**
*But I tell you of a truth, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elias, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when great famine was throughout all the land*

Ahab, having been searching for Elijah this whole time to get the prophet to undo the curse Israel was under is off searching again for Elijah, and with him his chief steward Obadiah.

They separate, and Elijah comes upon Obadiah who knows him well. Obadiah is a saved believer in the Lord, yet he works for the wicked king and queen.

Elijah tells Obadiah to fetch Ahab and tell him he's returned, and Obadiah fears for his life. He has been, this entire time, hiding his faith, just as he has his the prophets of the Lord in caves to keep them from Jezebel.

Rather than standing up to evil, preaching against Baal and sin, to bring Israel back to the Lord, they've been shut up in caves and Obadiah's paranoia at the possibility of Elijah ghosting him shows the level of fear of man, and not the fear of the Lord he claims to have.

This is similar to the way many Christians today hide their faith and fear tribulation and persecution more than they fear God. God may have used those hundred prophets to bring about revival. But they hid rather than face death.

**Matthew 10:28**
*And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.*

But Elijah assures Obadiah he will speak to the king that day, and when they return Ahab accuses Elijah of being responsible for the famine. Elijah corrects the wicked king, that it is he and his father's sin that brought it about. And Elijah challenged Ahab to being all Israel together and the prophets of Baal, and meet him at Mt Carmel.

There Elijah challenged the people of Israel; *How long halt ye between two opinions? if the Lord be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him.*

Then, as now, people generally are unwilling to commit to faith. They go along to get along and put off the choice of salvation or damnation if they can, usually to their own destruction.

The purpose of the word of the Lord is to bring people the choice and force them to decide; do they want to accept the truth? Eternal life in Christ Jesus, admitting they are sinners deserving death and taking the gracious gift of God? Or do they want to reject God and be given up, and given over. Twice-dead.

There are saved people in the world. There are slightly fewer reprobates (although that number seems to be growing). There is a vast majority of those who are caught between, often and in indecision. Soul-winning, giving the gospel to the unbelievers forces them to make this choice. And many receive it gladly. But others, it's the final straw before they decide they do not wish to retain God in their knowledge. And it's too late, reprobate.

Elijah is putting this same decision in the hands of the people.

And as a sign, Elijah calls for two pyres to be set up, two altars, with bullocks upon each as sacrifice. He challenges the 450 priests of Baal to call down fire from their god, to burn up the sacrifice.

And these priests called and called and danced and prayed and from morning until noon cried out 'O Baal, hear us!' But there was, of course, no answer.

teachings.title: The Romans Road gospel presentation
teachings.summary: The Romans Road with John 3:16 uses scripture to explain simply that all have sinned, Christ died for us, and whosoever believes and calls on the Lord is saved.
teachings.text:
*For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son that whosoever believeth on him shall not perish, but have everlasting life.*

*For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;*

*As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one*

*Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned*

*For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.*

*But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.*

*That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.*

*For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.*

This is the "Roman's Road," a short but direct use of scripture taken from the epistle to the Romans, as well as **John 3:16**, the most recognized verse in the Bible, and used by evangelists to win souls to the Lord for generations. It uses the word of God to explain the simple Gospel of salvation, that by hearing, a person may believe unto righteousness.

*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*

It is not the only means of giving the Gospel, but it is one of the most effective. It covers all the bases. Many times we may have to turn to other scripture to overcome objections or questions, but for the average person this is sufficient to explain Biblical salvation.

God loves the world and gave His only begotten Son that whosoever believeth on him shall not perish, but have eternal life. Everlasting.

That we need salvation because we all sin. That the punishment for sin is death and Hell. But the gift of God is eternal life in His Son. That while we are sinners, Christ still died for us. That if we believe this in our hearts and trust on God's promise, calling upon His holy name, we will be saved.

That's the Gospel.

teachings.title: The word is nigh thee
teachings.summary: Salvation is simply confessing Jesus as Lord and believing God raised Him, with no works or sacraments, so we must preach it.
teachings.text:
And so, Paul using Deuteronomy, familiar scripture to the believing Jews receiving his epistle to the churches at Rome, shows that the receiving of the law through Moses was the understanding of Christ.

And that understanding of Christ is put into one of the most beautiful passages of scripture, testifying to the salvation that is by faith on Jesus, and the truth of the nature of the Gospel.

*But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach; That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation. For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed. For there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek: for the same Lord over all is rich unto all that call upon him. For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.*

That's the simplicity of the Gospel. That's all of the law of faith. This is the righteousness of God that we obtain through Christ by faith, summed up. Complete.

There is no other way to Him except by this. There are no works, no special boy status, no secret traditions, ordinances, sacraments or other deeds of the law. And knowing this, then we must preach this glad tiding, this good news, that others may by the power of God's word, hear, believe and confess unto salvation.

*How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!*

teachings.title: If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean
teachings.summary: The leper calling on Jesus pictures the gospel: acknowledging our sickness of spirit and calling on Christ in faith today to be made clean.
teachings.text:
*Jesus, moved with compassion.* The leper believes, and calls upon Jesus to heal him, and Jesus, moved with compassion does so.

This is the purest form of the Gospel. The mercy and grace of Jesus' compassion on us, who in faith call upon His name and are made whole. He being the sacrifice for atonement. He being the blood shed for remission of our sins. Now, no longer the picture of Christ to come with the blood of bulls and goats in the law of Moses, but of His precious blood, sprinkled on the Mercy Seat.

Jesus have mercy on me, a sinner.

Acknowledging we are sick in spirit as the leper was in the flesh. And in the same faith, calling out to Him, "*If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean."*

If you believe that in your heart, call upon His name. Right where you are, today. Don't wait, for *The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.*

teachings.title: How can I, except some man guide me
