teachings.summary: God sent Philip to the Ethiopian eunuch to show that He will move heaven and earth to bring the gospel to any sincere seeker, answering the question of the man who never heard.
teachings.text:
Now Philip is called by the Lord to go to the desert of Gaza, and being obedient, he goes. He is called to do a great thing because he had shown God his commitment. The more we do for God the more He gives us to do, and so Philip gets this opportunity to show us how soul winning is done.

We meet the Ethiopian eunuch, who we are told was the queen of Ethiopia treasurer, and that she and he were followers of the Hebrew religion, or what the modern form of Pharisees it has taken.

He's reading scripture when Philip comes upon him, and providence has it, verses of Elijah that prophesizes Jesus.

We see the elegance of God's word, that Jesus is Christ revealed throughout scripture.

He asks the eunuch if he understands the scripture he's reading, and the reply is so true; unsaved people need saved people to explain scripture. "How can I unless a man guide me?" He is a receptive man, searching for truth.

This is an excellent example of how God will move heaven and earth to get the gospel to someone earnestly contending for the truth that is written in every man's heart. It is an answer to the natural man scoffing question "What about the savage in the jungle, hmm? Are they damned for not being born where they can hear about Jesus?"

Ask and ye shall receive. All men are called to Christ. Few who answer.

teachings.title: Whom shall I fear: boldness to win souls
teachings.summary: Saved by the Lord we have nothing to fear from men, yet many Christians fear knocking doors while missionaries face prison, and slogans on t-shirts are no bold stand.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 27** continues the pattern of praise for the salvation found in the Lord, by faith.

The Lord is our light and salvation. Jesus is the way, the truth and the light. We who have trusted in Him, are kept by the power of God unto salvation. What do we have to fear from men?

**Luke 12:4–5**
*And I say unto you my friends, Be not afraid of them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do. But I will forewarn you whom ye shall fear: Fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; yea, I say unto you, Fear him.*

The wicked who may seek your life cannot do anything but threaten you with Heaven. Whatever battle we face, we are already on the winning side. All in Christ have overcome this world. We can be confident in this, unto death.

And praise God we aren't in a time where we face constant war and battles. That our greatest fight is spiritual. And against our own flesh.

But there are those in the mission field, in countries where you can be beaten, imprisoned and killed for the cause of Christ. Meek and humble men and women who do great things for the Lord, daily. Winning souls and spreading the word of God in the face of persecution, without fear.

Many Christians today won't even venture into safe suburban neighborhoods once a week to do the same. Often, out of fear.

The fear of being a peculiar person. Of being socially rejected for the audacity of preaching Jesus to strangers. Of the "danger" of someone mocking you, or shutting the door in your face.

David believed, and it was sufficient to face legions of enemies. To face a giant with a sling. Missionaries and their converts face arrest and imprisonment, beatings and death.

American Christians wear "Faith Over Fear" graphic tees to the gym and think they are making a bold stand for Christ.

We should be boldly proclaiming the trust we have in a mighty God and the reward He has promised through the Son. *Though war should rise against me, in this will I be confident.*

teachings.title: The parable of the watchman
teachings.summary: Every saved Christian is a watchman responsible to warn others of judgment, and those not warned have their blood required at his hand.
teachings.text:
**Ezekiel 33** contains a lot of doctrine, and is one of the most often cited chapters of the prophet. Due to time and density, I will break it down over a few days.

The Parable of the Watchman is told in verses 1-9, and the idea of being a watchman, warning for danger is given, a trope used earlier in **Ezekiel 3**;

If you recall, God appoints Ezekiel as a watchman for the house of Israel, instructing him to warn the people of God’s judgment. If Ezekiel warns the wicked and they do not turn, their blood is on their own heads. If he fails to warn them, their blood is on his hands.

**Ezekiel 3:17**
*Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me*.

Here, in **Ezekiel 33**, the word of the Lord establishes this be understood to all the watchmen appointed to warn of the impending judgment, coming in the form of Babylon. The sword which is coming against Judah for her sin.

A good watchman sounds the trumpet, notifying the people of danger, and should they not heed it, the watchman is free from their blood.

But if the watchman doesn't sound the horn, he carries the blood of all those he could have warned.

In the days of siege warfare and raids, this was serious stuff. And again, in OT days, quite literal.

In the New Testament we are given these parables and stories for our own admonition and to teach us spiritual things, as Paul's application in **Acts** shows us, warning others about death and Hell, the coming judgment, removes their blood from our heads.

Soul-winning, or rather soul warning, is a responsibility for all saved Christians. That whenever we have the opportunity, we should be sounding the alarm. Blowing the trumpet. Warning others of the danger of an unregenerate life. Paul says he has done this, and is pure of the blood of all men.

When we miss opportunity to warn others, to share the gospel, we are like the watchman who fails to sound the alarm. Derelict Christians. And those who we could have warned and didn't, God says *his blood will I require at the watchman's hand*.

When we go out into the highways and hedges to compel others to come to the Lord, or tell our friends and family about eternal life and damnation, we cannot force them to accept the invitation. That is between the Spirit and them.

But we can and must warn them.

teachings.title: Be pure of the blood of all men
teachings.summary: Everyone can spare a few hours a week to go soul-winning with a church, so warn souls rather than pass by the burning house.
teachings.text:
I know it weighs heavy on my heart the number of people I have passed on giving the gospel too. The regret of hearing someone you know died, that you never warned. Feeling that blood on your head. I think every Christian, even babes in Christ, have had this feeling.

"Oh, how I wish I had warned them!" is a common lament.

How much more then should we feel that burden when we don't go soul-winning? When given a church, an opportunity to door knock, and we don't go?

It's one thing to wake to a fire in your own house, and warn your family to flee. But if you passed the home of strangers, and saw a fire spreading, wouldn't you bang on the door to get them to evacuate?

Or would you pass on by, leaving them to burn?

We cannot reach everyone. It would be difficult to quit our jobs, abandon our family and make evangelizing the world out only purpose. But everyone can spare a few hours a week to go soul-winning.

If you aren't part of a church, join one, even if it is for this sole purpose.

Organized door knocking is more profitable, and having a place to send the souls won to be taught all things and be baptized is crucial.

If you go to church, and they don't have soul-winning, ask the pastor to start a program. Offer to organize it. There are faithful people who would make excellent watchmen, sitting on the sidelines for lack of a program.

Warn souls. Be pure of the blood of all men.

teachings.title: Get over yourself and go door-knocking
teachings.summary: Ezekiel obeyed far harder commands without hesitation, so Christians should overcome fear and pride and give the gospel.
teachings.text:
The Lord tells Ezekiel to shave his head bald, and his beard, and divide the hair in three that he may burn a third, smite a third with a knife and scatter a third to the wind. This represents His judgment on the people.

Remember, from the beginning God has told Ezekiel to do these things among the children of Israel, in the captivity, that they may come to repentance. But, as He said they are a rebellious people and won't listen.

The performative nature of these tasks set before Ezekiel are dramatic. Some, like his fasting on dung bread and laying on his sides, take place over a long period of time. This act, shaving his hair and using it as an example of the judgment of God, is quicker and more dramatic. All of it is designed to explicitly teach what God wants them to know, but like the parables of Christ, they must have seemed like outlandish and wild acts to those without an ear to hear. And as crazy as it seemed to others, Ezekiel did it all without hesitation.

God asks so much less of us, giving His word to the lost. Yet many Christians today will not go out of their way to give the gospel to others. Consider Ezekiel and the humility and obedience in the exercises he did to spread God's word, and get over yourself, your fear, your pride, and find a local church that goes door-knocking. Bear fruit. Be salt. Let your light so shine. Glorify God.

teachings.title: Soul winning is soul warning
teachings.summary: Like Ezekiel the watchman, believers who fail to warn the lost have their blood on their heads, so go soul-winning.
teachings.text:
So, Ezekiel eats the scroll of the word of God, sweet as honey. And the Lord commissions Ezekiel to go among to the house of Israel, and to speak God's word to those in captivity with him in Babylon.

The Lord says that he is sending him among the people he knows and the language he speaks. Not among many strange people with many hard languages. But says if He had sent him to preach to them, they'd believe, but these Jews who should know better and understand his speech won't believe, because they are impudent and hardhearted. Hard headed. A rebellious house.

This reflects the eventual turn towards the Gentiles in the New Testament. That the Jews would not believe, and hardened their hearts, but the people who knew not God gladly accepted His word.

The appearance of the Lord departs, and the prophet goes to his home and he sat astonished at what had happened, for seven days.

Then the Lord came upon him again, and tells Ezekiel that he has been made a watchman unto the house of Israel, a theme that will carry throughout the book, and that has great relevance to saved believers today.

The watchman, upon the tower and the walls, is there to sound the trumpet in case of danger or attack, that in warning those in his charge, they may be prepared to act.

God says that if He says the wicked will surely die, and we don't warn them, his sins may be the reason but his blood is on our heads too.

And if you give warning, and they choose not to accept it, and act, then their blood isn't on you. You've done your part.

The Lord even clarifies further; not just the wicked who need to be warned, but the righteous, that their sin will lead them to death. That their works of righteousness won't be remembered. But our failure to warn them of this means we will bear some responsibility for it. We have to warn them, that even when they eventually sin (there is none righteous, no not one), they will still have eternal life having been warned, and believed God's word.

This is an awesome responsibility. It is the same great commission, given by Christ to all believers.

Many times you will hear preaching from soul-winning churches that what we really are doing is soul-warning, and it is so true. Only the person you're warning can take the gospel you give them, the Spirit working on them, and believe. But when we fail to warn people, their blood really is on our heads. Go soul-winning.

teachings.title: Be as bold and meek as Isaiah
teachings.summary: Isaiah went naked three years to preach God's point, so we clothed in Christ's righteousness should not be embarrassed to win souls.
teachings.text:
In the year that Sargon of Akkad, King of Assyria, sent his general Tartan to take Philistine city of Ashdod, the word of the Lord came upon Isaiah. And the Lord instructed Isaiah to go about naked and barefoot, for 3 years. This as a sign to how the Assyrian empire would take Egypt and Ethiopia captive, leading their people away the same.

The pride and glory of these nations would be brought low by the vessel God chose, Assyria. Just as Samaria and Assyria would be brought low by Babylon, and Judah led away into captivity.

Isaiah, with great humility, obeyed the Lord. Naked, without shoes, for years to preach a point of God.

How many of us have the opportunity to share God's truth with others, and being embarrassed hold back? Or say nothing?

Fully clothed, even clothed in the righteousness of Christ Jesus, we still shy away from preaching His word.

Let us be as bold and meek as Isaiah. Praise God and win souls, warning them of the coming destruction that every man faces without Jesus.

teachings.title: Don't make God send the storm
teachings.summary: Christians who run from preaching like Jonah are still used by God, so stop running and dedicate yourself to soul winning.
teachings.text:
It is funny how, despite Jonah not wanting to preach the Lord to the heathen, he still manages to get the men of Joppa to believe on the Lord God. He is literally the worst prophet and yet God uses him mightily.

Often Christians are reluctant to preach the word to others. We bury our talent of silver. We put our light under a bushel. We flee to Tarshish, running to the things of this world seeking to avoid our responsibility. And even in our dereliction, God uses us to proclaim His truth. How much more so if we let Him shape us into worthy vessels?

We shouldn't need to be swallowed up by a whale to be dragged back to where we need to be to do God's will. But if that's what it takes, He won't hesitate.

It is hard to kick against the pricks, as Jesus said to Saul on the road to Damascus. The Bible says to know to do good and to do it not is a sin.

Make this new year the year you dedicate yourself to doing the will of the Lord. To soul-winning and preaching His word, even to your enemies. To stop running away.

Don't make God send the storm.

teachings.title: Never be ashamed to preach the word
teachings.summary: As the Jews threatened the prophets and killed Christ, the world will hate Christians who preach God's word, but we must boldly share the gospel and never be ashamed of it.
teachings.text:
**John 5:14-18**
*Afterward Jesus findeth him in the temple, and said unto him, Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee. The man departed, and told the Jews that it was Jesus, which had made him whole. And therefore did the Jews persecute Jesus, and sought to slay him, because he had done these things on the sabbath day. But Jesus answered them, My Father worketh hitherto, and I work. Therefore the Jews sought the more to kill him, because he not only had broken the sabbath, but said also that God was his Father, making himself equal with God.*

**Matthew 23:35-38**
*That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar. Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation. O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not! Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.*

Just as the Jews frequently sought the life of Jesus, before finally killing Him on the cross, they would frequently threaten the life of the prophets, killing many.

But yet they preached the word of God. And, sometimes, they were blessed with the knowledge that the people listened and the rulers relented, and turning from their wicked ways, God repented of the evil He would do to them.

Today, worldly people who despise God and His judgment will react in the same way to Christians who preach the word of God. Who give the gospel to the lost. Who stand in the gap. Who affirm the perfect word of God in season or out of season.

But there are many who will hear His word, believe on it and repent towards God.

We cannot be afraid to share the good news. We can't hide our light under a bushel. We have to take what He has whispered in our ear and shout it from the rooftops.

And if they seek your life for it, rejoice. It is to God's glory. And if you win souls to Christ, it is to God's glory.

But never be ashamed to preach the word of God.

**Romans 1:16**
*For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.*

teachings.title: The righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith
teachings.summary: When believers share the gospel, God reveals His righteousness through them, an awesome responsibility for every saved Christian.
teachings.text:
And Paul makes the important distinction that while it was to the Jew first, it is also to the Greek, or the Gentiles, the other nations. That it is for **every one** who believes.

And the sharing of that power of God contains His righteousness, to be revealed to us, faith to faith. As we share the Gospel and win souls by the power of His word, God reveals His righteousness to the world.

This is important.

God has revealed to us His good news, the power of salvation, by the prophets, in the scriptures, by the life and death and resurrection of Jesus, His son, and now by the power of the Gospel, given by those who believe unto others that may believe. It is a revelation into the very nature of God to understand that the just shall live by faith.

Paul is going to further break down the revelations of God, how He reveals Himself to us that we may better understand Him, but this one is the most important.

When we share the Gospel to others, we are an instrument that reveals the nature of God to others. His righteousness.

And so, when we live blameless as we can, staying in the word, in prayer without ceasing for our brethren, praying for the will of God in Jesus' name, all to be a good example and rightly judge, that we may have fruit by winning souls, or be edifying, a comfort to others who share our faith, we are able to better serve Him, and be part of that revelation of Him to the world.

We magnify His love and mercy. We demonstrate the power of His gift. We are the light that draws men to Him. We are partakers in His divine revelation.

That is an awesome responsibility and a blessing greater than any other in this life.

teachings.title: I know whom I have believed
teachings.summary: Paul, in chains, urges Timothy not to be ashamed of the gospel, teaching that predestination is in Christ, not of individual believers, and resting in the assurance that God keeps what we commit to Him.
teachings.text:
The introduction to this letter to Timothy, which Paul is writing from Rome, under house arrest, chained to a centurion day and night. We learn that Timothy got saved following his grandmother and mother to Christ, and was given the gifts of the Holy Ghost by the laying on of hands by Paul, an Apostle indeed.

In his bonds, Paul shares that it is memories of things like Timothy's accepting of the Gospel that bring joy to him while in his predicament, and to encourage Timothy and others who may read this epistle to be of good cheer, hopeful in Christ and not ashamed of Paul's status.

*For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.*

He goes on to embolden Timothy, not to be ashamed of the Gospel, to lean on the power of the Holy Ghost upon him. To be a partaker of the persecution Paul suffers, willingly, because it is to the glory of God and the furtherance of the Gospel.

Paul says to Timothy that God has called them, *called us with an holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before the world began,* *But is now made manifest by the appearing of our Saviour Jesus Christ*.

Note it is the predestination of Jesus Christ, not of the believer, that brings us to be used by God for His purpose, now that Christ was made manifest in Jesus, who abolished death and revealed immortality through the good news. The Gospel.

This is how predestination works. Foreknowledge by God, predestinated in Christ, fufifiled in our belief, conformed to His use.

*For the which cause I also suffer these things: nevertheless I am not ashamed: for I know whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day.*

Blessed assurance. We hold the ernest of His promise in our quickened spirit, the Holy Ghost indwelling within. Even in his persecution and humiliation, Paul knows the victory already won. He will not be ashamed for having placed his faith in the living God.

**Romans 10:11**
*For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed*.

Paul needs to write this encouraging word because of the betrayal of some in the faith, who having regarded his predicament, abandoned Paul. Not speaking out for him, and in fact turned away from the Apostle. Phygellus and Hermogenes are named in scripture, to their everlasting shame.

But, not being a downer, Paul also gives praise to Onesiphorus for seeking him out and refreshing him in Paul's afflictions. Mercy and honor from God for being unashamed of the faith during tribulation.

We should pray we can be like Paul, or at the very least Onesiphorus, when tribulations come.

teachings.title: The gospel came in power and in the Holy Ghost
teachings.summary: The Thessalonians show the Great Commission bearing fruit, the gospel spreading everywhere within years by the power of the Holy Ghost in those who preached it.
teachings.text:
From the risen Christ in **Matthew 28**, giving the Great Commission to His Apostles;

*All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth. Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you always, even unto the end of the world. Amen.*

Here, in **1 Thessalonians 1**, we see the fruit of this command to give the Gospel to every creature play out.

Paul, Silvanus and Timothy, writing to the church in Thessalonica, hailing them "*in God the Father and in the Lord Jesus Christ,*" write about their work for the Lord in spreading the same Gospel that they received from Paul and the other evangelists, throughout Asia Minor.

*For our gospel came not unto you in word only, but also in power, and in the Holy Ghost, and in much assurance; as ye know what manner of men we were among you for your sake.*

*Ye became followers of us, and of the Lord, having received the word in much affliction, with joy of the Holy Ghost. So that ye were ensamples to all that believe in Macedonia and Achaia. For from you sounded out the word of the Lord not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but also in every place your faith to God-ward is spread abroad; so that we need not to speak any thing.*

It is amazing that within a few years of Christ's resurrection and ascension, churches had sprung up throughout the world, dedicated to the same Gospel as He preached, and the prophets gave witness too. A light shining out into the world leading all men to repent towards *the living and true God;*

*And to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead, even Jesus, which delivered us from the wrath to come.*

To understand the power of the word as it is given, and that power a testimony of its truth, is to understand how it would be possible to convince so many disparate peoples to come to the saving faith in Christ, not from firsthand account or witness, but by the Holy Ghost moving in those spreading the good news *in every place your faith to God-ward is spread abroad; so that we need not to speak any thing.*

Living faith to faith. Building the body of Christ. Amen

teachings.title: Cast thy bread upon the waters
teachings.theme: Sowing the seed of the word
teachings.summary: Since we know not what tomorrow brings, give liberally and sow the word at every opportunity, boldly preaching Christ, and it shall not return void.
teachings.text:
The Preacher, Solomon, is beginning to wrap up his homily. He has built his case, that while life is vain, and full of vexing things, toil and tribulation, that God blesses us to enjoy the fruits of our labor. And that God blesses the wise and prudent more than the wicked and fools.

The chapter begins with an appeal to generosity. Casting your bread on the waters. Giving liberally to others, and guarding against an uncertain future. It will return to you in like measure. And you can't take it with you. Who knows what tomorrow may bring?

Whatever will be will be. If the clouds bring rain, or a tree falls in the forest with no one to see, it still is what it is. And so is life. Natural events occur without our ability to predict or change.

**James 4:13-15**
*Go to now, ye that say, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain: Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away. For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that.*

We should then make the most of it, and God willing, enjoy the blessings He provides with thanksgiving. Hospitality. Generosity. Charity towards all, regardless of the conditions we find ourselves in.

Don't wait for a perfect opportunity to do right and live well. *He that observeth the wind shall not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap.* Take what you are given and act.

We don't understand the miracle of life, the ways of God, let alone the ideal circumstances for our best laid plans. Remember, time and chance happen to us all. Death comes for us all.

Sow your seed in the morning and evening and at every opportunity, and give the rest to God.

Spiritually, this includes the seed that is the word, and laying up treasure in Heaven. Be ready at any opportunity to give the gospel.

**Isaiah 55:11**
*So shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it.*

Jesus is the bread of life. Cast His word on many waters, and see it return again unto you. Boldly preach salvation in the name of Jesus Christ. Be a cheerful giver with what you have in this world. Be it food or wealth or the truth of Christ.

teachings.title: Naaman and the seed by the way side
teachings.theme: Sowing the seed of the word
teachings.summary: Like Naaman, many who hear the gospel confess it in the moment but never receive it in their hearts, as the seed sown by the way side.
teachings.text:
Here in **2 Kings 5**, we find the Syrian captain, Naaman, stricken with the incurable disease, leprosy. And a servant girl, captive out of Israel, tells Namaan's wife of the prophet of the Lord in Samaria, that is Israel.

With permission of his king and loaded with treasure, Naaman and servants go into the King of Israel, asking he be recovered of his leprosy.

The king becomes upset, thinking this is a trap. How can he heal a man of something that is untreatable? The King of Syria would hold it against him, he rends his clothes in distress.

Elisha heard of this and sends for Naaman, and when the Syrian comes to him, the prophet's servant comes to him with a message; Wash yourself in the Jordan seven times and be healed.

At first, Naaman is offended. He expected the man of God to come and lay hands and make a show and heal him there in the spot. He questions why he just go to the Jordon, when Syrian rivers are superior in his mind, and more convenient.

But his servants convince him to try, and he does as the prophet said, and is healed. Cleaned of the leprosy.

He returns to Elisha, and confesses that now he believes there is no other God in all the earth, but in Israel. And he offers the treasure he has brought to the prophet.

Elisha refuses, in the name of the Lord.

Namaan asks then for two burdens of earth, soil from Israel, that he would make sacrifices of burnt offerings only to the Lord. As he had previously believed the waters of the rivers were different in Syria, now he assumes the mounds of Israeli dirt would matter in the sacrifice to God.

He also asks for pardon, for Elisha's blessing, that when he returned to Syria, that when he went in to the house of Rimmon, a temple to idols, and bow himself down, that the Lord forgive him. He is indicating that while he believes that the Lord is the only true God, he would still go before idols and bow down before them, because of custom and what others might think.

Asking for permission, and the Lord's blessing to be unfaithful to the Lord he proclaimed, Elisha offers nothing, but says "Go in peace."

Whether Naaman actually believed on the Lord is doubtful. He seemed caught up in the moment and the miracle that had occurred, and yet still carnal. Seeing the water as important, rather than following the word of God. Seeing the soil as different. Pledging with one hand to worship only the Lord, and at the other admit he would continue in the false religion of his people.

In many ways, this is the experience many have when given the Gospel. They are resistant to the truth, show doubt and disdain when told there is only one way to salvation, faith in Christ Jesus. They may taste of the Heavenly gifts as the Spirit works in them to help bring them to the truth. They may even confess that this IS the truth, and they promise they will do whatever it takes to convince God, the person who gave them the gospel, other Christians.

But in the end, they are already thinking about the ways they will back out of their promise. They are already back to their old beliefs before the words of the promise had come out of their mouths. They never accepted the truth in their hearts.

They are like the seed sown on the pathway in the parables of the Sower;

*Behold, a sower went forth to sow; And when he sowed, some seeds fell by the way side, and the fowls came and devoured them up*.

*When any one heareth the word of the kingdom, and understandeth it not, then cometh the wicked one, and catcheth away that which was sown in his heart. This is he which received seed by the way side.*

An all too common occurrence.

teachings.title: Give the gospel from scripture, not rhetoric
teachings.theme: Sowing the seed of the word
teachings.summary: Faith comes by hearing the word, so a true gospel presentation leads through scripture, while false prophets paraphrase to avoid being pinned down.
teachings.text:
Now [here](https://youtu.be/F8owXQ2QyvA) is the Gospel presentation that I took that screenshot from. Notice that the Pastor uses scripture to lead the listener through the Gospel.

The Bible says that faith comes by hearing the word of God. The power is in the word. God uses scripture to prick our hearts.

You see Philip with the eunuch expounds on who Christ is from scripture, guiding him. When Paul and Silas were with the Philipian jailer, who asks "What must I do to be saved," they say believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, *And they spake unto him the word of the Lord, and to all that were in his house.*

Oftentimes, when you see a false prophet attempting to give their version of what it takes to be saved (if they can be pinned down to do so) they don't use scripture, but rather their own paraphrasing rhetoric.

The scriptures are a rock. They do not change. But by avoiding direct reference to the Bible, they are able to avoid being pinned down, and can twist or add to Biblical concepts, such as appending "...of your sins" to every appearance of "repent."

**Romans 10:11-17**
*For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed. For there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek: for the same Lord over all is rich unto all that call upon him. For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things! But they have not all obeyed the gospel. For Esaias saith, Lord, who hath believed our report?*

*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*

teachings.title: Faith cometh by hearing the word
teachings.theme: Sowing the seed of the word
teachings.summary: Winning souls is the work of eternal value, and the power to save is in the preached word of God, not our arguments or tracts.
teachings.text:
Our entire purpose as vessels fit for righteousness, is spreading and sending others to spread the word of God, that He may have the increase. That the harvest, which is plentiful have laborers to bring in the sheaves. That we be servants of the Gospel. Ministers of His word.

**1 Corinthians 3:5-8**
*Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos, but ministers by whom ye believed, even as the Lord gave to every man? I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase. So then neither is he that planteth any thing, neither he that watereth; but God that giveth the increase. Now he that planteth and he that watereth are one: and every man shall receive his own reward according to his own labour.*

These are the works that matter. That have eternal value. That, unlike the wood, hay and stubble of our own vain works and filthy rags of our own righteousness which burn up, the winning of souls and edification of others that they may win souls are the precious stones, silver and gold that remain. The eternal value of those things we build up on the foundation that is Christ.

We must be sent, into the highways and hedges, preaching the Gospel to every creature, so that they may hear the word of God, and by hearing, believe, and by their faith, confess the truth with their mouths, that they too may be sent. This is the way.

Note the power is in the word we preach. The word of God found in scripture.

*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*

The power to save men's souls is in God's word. Not our logical arguments, not in our boasts or testimonials. Certainly not in our selfish acts of following the letter of the law, the vain traditions of men, washing the outside of the cup while the inside is filthy. But by scripture.

*Faith cometh by hearing and hearing by the word of God*, preached by those that believe, sent to gather for the harvest.

*For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.*

This is an important idea for saved Christians to grasp. That for all the efforts made to send people tracts, pocket New Testaments, door hangers and invitations to church, and our own attempts to get people to believe by our rephrasing and paraphrasing and using logic, none of it saves.

*Faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*

The power is in the word. The Spirit works through the word, given by believers to bring men to faith. And so we should not hide that light under a bushel. We should shout it from the rooftops.

*For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth*.

teachings.title: Not only saving souls but building them up
teachings.theme: Sowing the seed of the word
teachings.summary: Paul's care for the Thessalonians shows that after winning souls we must edify new believers like our own children to walk worthy of God.
teachings.text:
Continuing to exhort the church at Thessalonica, Paul reminds them of their conversion, repenting towards the Gospel, and of how Paul and his helpers behaved among them, just as they preached the truth of Christ Jesus in Philippi, a city a few hours west, in northern Greece.

It was there in Acts 16, where Paul and Silas are accused of causing "exceeding trouble" by those who protested the gospel being preached, and brought them before magistrates, had them scourged, and finally jailed Paul and Silas. All of which came to serve the glory of God even the more, getting their jailer and his family saved, and planting a church.

And we are told here, that it is this time in Philippi that the members of the church of Thessalonica would recognize how shamefully treated they were for their mission, and understand that they came to them boldly with the word of God, through much tribulation, without guile or flattery, but with the stripes of suffering and still proclaiming the truth. That they were willing to give them not just the Gospel, but give up their own lives to proclaim it, because it is truth, and out of the love they feel towards them that received it.

Paul then reminds them of how, like his own children, he gave them not just the good news of Christ that brought to them salvation and the Spirit, but further exhortation to live blamelessly, as is befitting a saved Christian. To walk worthy of the call they answered, worthy of the God that saved them.

A reminder that it is not just saving souls that we should do, but then building upon that salvation, encouraging and edifying babes in Christ, as we would our own children, to walk a Christian walk. Preaching against sin and towards the path of righteousness. Even in tribulation and contentions by man, but pleasing to God.

Paul compares them and their tribulation and persecution they are suffering to the churches in Judea, and their persecution by the Jews. Following after the churches in Christ, to be likewise afflicted, persecuted by the Macedonians, their fellow countrymen.

teachings.title: Converting to a denomination is not soul winning
teachings.theme: Sowing the seed of the word
teachings.summary: Winning people to a denomination's traditions and works-based grace is not soul winning; only the gospel of grace through faith in Christ gives a sure hope.
teachings.text:
I don't know who needs to hear this, but convincing someone to convert to your particular denomination, with how based and trad their services are, their vain traditions, architecture and earthly treasures, political power or philosophies and theologies of man, is not giving the Gospel and getting people saved.

You're not a soul winning by convincing people to believe your denomination's false doctrines of subscription-based Grace doled out through works, and finding out later if you did enough to merit heaven. That's not the simplicity of Christ, that is not the blessed hope found in Him.

It is only through giving the gospel of grace by faith, In Christ alone unto eternal salvation, the good news as proclaimed throughout the New Testament.

*Sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear:*

How do you say you have hope within you when you say to someone that maybe they were chosen, or maybe they'll do enough works, or maybe they'll stick with it till the end repenting of enough sins, and maybe they might have to go to mythical purgatory and suffer, because what Christ did wasn't sufficient for you.

That's not hope, and it certainly isn't meekness and it shows a lack of fear of God, adding to his word knowing the price that pays.

teachings.title: God shall likewise destroy thee for ever
teachings.summary: The boastful wicked who reject the fear of the Lord face eternal torment in hell, and believers should name them plainly and preach that hard truth so some may be pulled out of the fire.
teachings.text:
In **Psalm 52**, the psalmist presents the polar opposite of the contrite heart of **Psalm 51**, the mischief-making man who doesn't avail himself to the longsuffering mercy of God.

The wicked and their deceitful tongue, inventing lies, telling slander against God and God's people, boasting of their blessings, not thankful but vain in their imagination, loving evil more than good, these are the men who continually reject the call to fear the Lord.

Those of us who are saved can become incredulous at the prideful stance of the wicked, who reject the fear of God and lean on their own strength. We can often grow confounded and even depressed over the ways of the wicked. Like just Lot, living in Sodom, being afflicted by the wickedness around him

**2 Peter 2:8**
(*For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)*

The Bible is not afraid to call these people out, directly and to their face. They are boastful, mockingly called "mighty men," liars, evil, haters of righteousness, lovers of slanderous and wicked words, lovers of mischief, having deceitful tongues.

We should not fear to identify exactly the perverted in our midst when they reject and mock the gospel of God and the word we preach.

Nor should we tiptoe around the heart of the matter; Their immanent destruction and the torment in the fire of Hell that awaits them.

**Jude 1:22–23**
*And of some have compassion, making a difference: And others save with fear, pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh.*

Those who do not see the wrath of God revealed from Heaven upon others as a reason to repent and believe, and won't see the mercy and hear the praise of the meek, feeling the compassionate love of believers magnify God's grace, need hard preaching to let them know exactly what they've chosen, in hopes that they might be saved.

That their love of devouring words will lead to God likewise destroying them forever. Literally, being devoured by flame and worm in outer darkness, forever. Eternal suffering at the hands of a just and mighty God.

*God shall likewise destroy thee for ever, he shall take thee away, and pluck thee out of thy dwelling place, and root thee out of the land of the living.* *Selah*.

If "selah" is meant to be a pause, a moment to reflect on what was just sung or said, is there anywhere more fitting than in that moment, having heard that sobering truth?

God will destroy you. He will take your life and root you out of the land of the living, to place you in a place of eternal destruction.

And the righteous shall see their end and fear God, and laugh at the calamity they brought about on themselves. The end their mischief brought about, turned back upon them.

**Proverbs 26:27**
*Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him*.

The ironic nature of the bitter end experienced by the boastful sinner is often evident and clear to those that fear God. The humor of the Lord is appreciated by His children. We laugh at their calamity.

When the wicked are made a parable or a byword among the people, it should give other men pause. The wrath revealed from Heaven should give instruction to the simple to turn towards God. It shows the righteous in Christ God's power and promise.

**Proverbs 1:7**
*The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.*

The warning is ignored by the fool. And God will not be mocked.

**Proverbs 1:25–30**
*But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof: I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh; When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you. Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me: For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the LORD: They would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproof.*

teachings.title: Blessed is the man whose sin is covered
teachings.summary: As David and Paul teach, God imputes righteousness without works and does not hold the believer's sins against him, and this good news must be received today before God's Spirit ceases to strive.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 32** opens with a very familiar and important doctrine, the understanding of God's forgiveness for sin in the saved believer's life. This foundational fact is repeated by Paul in the letter to the Romans;

**Romans 4:6–8**
*Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin.*

The truth is that, in Christ, whether it was in David's day, or Paul's or our own, God forgives our past transgressions, covers our current sin, and will not hold our future sins and iniquity against us.

This positional standing of righteousness before God, despite our sins, through His imputed righteousness is made possible, through the Holy Spirit, by the renewal, the regeneration, the quickening of our spirit. The new man within us. Blessed is the man *in whose spirit there is no guile.*

We are given the Spirit of truth, that we may acknowledge our sin, knowing that we are forgiven of all sin, first, not by works but by faith.

The same good news today as in David's day. And this Psalm serves as an evangelical appeal.

David writes of a man who kept his silence, who hadn't called upon the name of the Lord, who suffered in their sins, bones waxing old and dried up by their roaring in the daytime, the heaviness of their iniquity weighing on them at night.

But the honesty and humility of acknowledging sin, not hiding anything from God (as if we could), confessing our transgressions unto the Lord, and being forgiven, is a blessing. Rioting in the daytime and being kept up at night by our conscience, being convicted in the Spirit, gives way to the peace that passes understanding, through the forgiveness that is given to us by God's mercy and grace.

David reminds us that there is a time where God may be sought, before it is too late.

**Isaiah 55:6**
*Seek ye the LORD while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near*

God's Spirit will not always strive with man. There comes a time when those that put off or reject the truth, not acknowledging that they are sinners, lying to God and themselves, are no longer able to come to Him. Where He no longer extends His hand, because they have hardened their hearts and will not seek Him, even as they face destruction.

**Hebrews 4:7**
*Again, he limiteth a certain day, saying in David, To day, after so long a time; as it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts.*

We have the example of those in the days of Noah, who mocked him for his faith in preparing the ark, and whose disobedient spirits who Christ preached to in Hell, were destroyed by the flood, never coming nigh unto God. Just as those left to God's wrath to come will not repent, despite the horrors of His judgment.

There is a time, it is today. There is a day, and it is the present. If you haven't accepted the truth that we are sinners in need of salvation, and that it is offered as a free gift to all who believe, through the grace of Almighty God, now is the time.

**2 Corinthians 6:2**
*(For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)*

teachings.title: Our testimony in persecution leads others to seek Him
teachings.summary: The daughters who asked what made her beloved special now seek him with her, showing that a believer's faithful testimony through trials leads others to Christ.
teachings.text:
The daughters of Jerusalem chorus in chapter 5 asked of the woman; *What is thy beloved more than another beloved, O thou fairest among women?*

The chapter ends with the woman, battered and bloody from the world's treatment of her for his sake, extolling his virtues and singing praise to his perfection.

The character arc from the ecstatic bride at the feast to the complacent woman, making excuses to avoid her love, then realizing and searching him out again, only to be mistreated by the watchmen and questioned by the daughters, and ultimately to still profess her love and devotion for Jesus, is a wonderful picture of things that can and do happen in the Christian life.

And her faith through the trials leads others to seek Him.

Chapter 6 opens with the same chorus of daughters, and they have changed their tune.

*Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? whither is thy beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with thee.*

Our testimony, especially in persecution, not only reestablishes our faith, but leads others to seek Jesus.

We can often feel adrift. We may realize we should do more for the cause of Christ. We may have a sense of separation from Him. We may call out in prayer as David did:

**Psalms 51:12**
*Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.*

But we should be aware that as saved Christians, seeking to get back on the right path, we will see persecution. The devil will attempt to sift us like wheat. Satan doesn't need much to keep the unsaved from seeking truth, but he works overtime to keep Christians from being fruitful.

So, having persuaded the daughters, the woman answers them; that she knows where her beloved has gone. He is down in His garden, to feed the garden and gather lilies. A picture of the gospel light, the harvest of believers, the fruit of His good pleasure.

She affirms her faith; *I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine: he feedeth among the lilie*s, and then the narrator shifts again to the King.

He praises his beloved, comparing her beauty to Tirzah, a city known for its natural beauty, and even as Jerusalem, ready for war, filled with bannermen, armies ready to march.

He is overwhelmed with her beauty, repeating the verses poetically comparing her hair and teeth to goats and sheep as the lyrics from chapter 4.

He numbers her among 60 queens and 80 concubines and countless virgins, a royal harem, and says she alone is above them all. Undefiled. The choice daughter, whom all the other women blessed and praised. Beloved above them all.

Verse 10, the daughters of Jerusalem, the very courtesans the King compared his beloved to, sing her praises.

*Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners?*

We are His beloved. We are the light of the world. We shine forth to all nations, calling them to Christ. Provoking them to envy, that they may seek to be His bride.

The woman sings in verse 11, that she has gone down to her beloved's garden. To see the fruit of the garden, and if the vine flourished, Jesus is the true vine. She's returned to His rest, as quickly as the chariots, to her beloved, upon seeing the bounty of his garden.

The daughters encourage her, *Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look upon thee.* And her beloved asks them *What will ye see in the Shulamite? As it were the company of two armies.* A refrain answered in the next chapter.

teachings.title: Wisdom maketh his face to shine
teachings.summary: Walking with God and being anointed by the Spirit changes a believer's countenance and gives boldness to preach the truth, so that others see they have been with Jesus.
teachings.text:
The Preacher continues his sermon. Having said he has searched for wisdom by observation of all things under the Sun, and having found all have sinned and fallen short. That the wise and the fool, the rich and the poor, all are appointed to die, and after this, judged and found wanting, that then the only way is God's. That fear of Him and seeking His favor is the only alternative to the vanity and vexation of spirit that man travails in.

Solomon begins **Ecclesiastes 8** praising the effect that seeking God's wisdom has on us. That it makes the face to shine, and to speak boldly His truth. That it changes the countenance of a person to walk with God.

**Exodus 34:29-30**
*And it came to pass, when Moses came down from mount Sinai with the two tables of testimony in Moses' hand, when he came down from the mount, that Moses wist not that the skin of his face shone while he talked with him. And when Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone; and they were afraid to come nigh him.*

Moses had to cover his face from the people, it disturbed them so much to see the radiance coming from his time with God.

**Psalm 104:15**
*And wine that maketh glad the heart of man, and oil to make his face to shine, and bread which strengtheneth man's heart*.

The Spirit is described as oil, which anoints us as we walk in Him. The bread, His word. Our heart, merry from the juice of the vine, which is Christ. He does make our faces shine. His light magnified through us, that men see us and know, we have been with Jesus. And the boldness of our wisdom comes from the confidence we have in Him and His word.

The Spirit filled the disciples of Christ, gathered in the upper room on Pentecost, and having His anointing, they went out among the multitudes gathered for the feast in Jerusalem, and preached with boldness.

Acts 2:1-4
*And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place. And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting. And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance*.

The men, hearing the miracle of preaching Christ from scripture, in their own tongues, languages from around the known world, they wondered; *Behold, are not all these which speak Galilaeans?* But the disciples had been changed by their time with God. The boldness to preach Christ from scripture, and 3,000 souls came to repentance.

Just as when Peter and John were brought before the religious leaders of the Jews for preaching Christ, these lowly fishermen gave witness that they had been with Christ by their boldness.

**Acts 4:13**
*Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.*

Their light so shined, that others saw and praised God. The anointing of the Spirit, the truth of God's word, the wisdom they trusted, gave them boldness to preach the truth. They were changed.

The understanding that man's countenance gives away their time with God to others, has a counterpoint in scripture. That the reprobate, those that hold the truth in unrighteousness, have a similar change;

**Isaiah 3:9**
*The shew of their countenance doth witness against them; and they declare their sin as Sodom, they hide it not. Woe unto their soul! for they have rewarded evil unto themselves.*

We should seek to walk with God, to be anointed with the Spirit, that men look upon us and take note that we have been with Jesus. To speak boldly the wisdom of the gospel. To make known the truth of His way.

teachings.title: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper
teachings.summary: With freedom to preach openly, Christians still hide, and believers must confess and forsake their sins, including neglect of church, Bible and soul winning, rather than harden their hearts.
teachings.text:
Moving on: When the righteous men rejoice, there is great glory. When God has blessed His people with leaders who openly praise His name, we have the opportunity for glory. But when the wicked men rise, the righteous are hidden.

Tying this again to soul-winning, evangelizing to the lost, praising God's name in the open, or even reading the Bible and speaking His word confidently, is easy in modern America, today. We have the freedom to openly glorify God. Our leaders, even if they are wolves and deceivers, pay lip service to the Lord and believers are able to openly proclaim Christ without fear.

Yet so many men are hidden, still. It's a shame that many churches do not have any soul-winning. That many Christians hide who they are, and what Jesus has done for them. That so few read the Bible here, while there are countries where reading scripture can be a prison sentence. That confessing Christ can end in death.

Maybe it is a parallel to the rich young man. That by our comfort and safety we grow complacent. Maybe revival requires tribulation. Maybe the embarrassment of riches we have in the freedom we've been granted by God has caused too many Christians to have their heart hardened for the lost.

Vs 13; *He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.*

We know that in Christ our sins are forgiven, past, present and future. But we are also to faithfully confess our sins to the Father, Who is faithful again to forgive.

Covering sin leads to the chastening of the Lord. Humbling ourselves to admit our failings will have mercy.

Keeping the theme going, you can see how those Christians who don't go to church, don't read their Bible, don't spread the gospel, would rather hide their sin than acknowledge and foresake them. If they confess, they're conceding to God that they know better, and if they agree that His way is the way forward, then they cannot continue on in theirs.

They become paralyzed by their own guilty conscience and love of their sin.

"If I go to church, I am admitting I should, and so now I am on the hook to keep going." Same with Bible reading, prayer, or evangelizing.

We read in vs 9 that if you hate hearing the law because you want to continue doing the things God says you shouldn't, even your prayers shall be abominations.

How much worse are our prayers when we have the liberty to go to church, to get plugged in, to hear hard preaching, to learn God's word, to hear the law and confess our sins and be forgiven, and have the freedom to joyfully tell others the riches of God, and yet we ignore it all?

Is it any wonder we end up with a wicked ruler will rise up over a spiritually poor people? To take away the things and riches we take for granted? To provoke God's people to turn again to Him and do what's right, that He may heal the land?

V 14-15 seem to be separate points, yet in this larger context they reveal a greater truth;

*Happy is the man that feareth alway: but he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief. As a roaring lion, and a ranging bear; so is a wicked ruler over the poor people.*

Don't harden your hearts. Humble yourself. Confess your sins, including those that come from omissions. To know to do good and to do it not. Return to the first love. Obey the Great Commission. We have been given the ministry of reconciliation, and the opportunity to be servants to the Lord. Don't squander it. Redeem the time. Repent, ask forgiveness and turn to the paths of the Lord.

teachings.title: Deliver them that are drawn unto death
teachings.summary: Every man is judged by his works, believers at the bema seat for reward and the lost at the Great White Throne, so a believer who fails to give the gospel to the perishing cannot plead ignorance and will suffer loss.
teachings.text:
Continuing the fatherly advice of the King, Solomon, to his son the prince,  **Proverbs 24:11-12**;

*If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain; If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?*

He says that failure to deliver someone marked for death by claiming ignorance to the circumstances, and potentially the injustice or false accusations that led to it, by not hearing the matter fully - that it is not an excuse. Solomon writes that we should consider our own soul, the Lord's mercy upon it, His judgment. That He will judge every man according to his works.

This is echoed in the New Testament.

**Romans 2:4-9**
*Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance? But after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God; Who will render to every man according to his deeds: To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life: But unto them that are contentious, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and wrath, Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile*

**Hebrews 9:27**
*And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment.*

The wages of sin is death. We are all guilty. We will all be judged. But those in faith, who have believed on Christ, our sins not being imputed against our record, being justified by the righteousness of Jesus, our works, being built upon that foundation, are judged at the bema seat of Christ, to see what sort of works they are.

**1 Corinthians 3:12-15**
*Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.*

We are still saved, but, based on the criteria of God; the good will be rewarded and the vain and meaningless, destroyed.

Meanwhile, the unbelieving are judged by their works at the Great White Throne. Their works held against them;

**Revelation 20:11-15**
*And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them. And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works. And the sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them: and they were judged every man according to their works. And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death. And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.*

With this perspective, which Solomon clearly understood, a ruler must make the effort to know what he is judging, especially in a capital crime where a life hangs in jeopardy.

This warning applies to those that are princes by faith, in the Kingdom of God. To believers, every man we meet is appointed to death and Hell for their sins. They are drawn unto death, and ready to be slain.

If we forbear to deliver them, to give them the gospel, we cannot say we didn't know. He that pondereth the heart and keepeth our soul, He knows it. And it will be counted a loss in the trying fire at the judgment seat of Christ.

teachings.title: Cast not your pearls before swine
teachings.summary: Fools despise wisdom, so whether online or soul winning door to door we should give our piece, reject the heretic after admonition, shake off the dust and not be trapped in debate.
teachings.text:
Next, we are told to not speak wisdom to the fool, for they despise it. They do not value wise words, or that which is holy;

**Matthew 7:6**
*Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.*

Jesus' words against giving the word of God to dogs and swine, the sodomites and the reprobate, is an escalation to the proverb. Just as we will see, arguing with fools and the wicked is vanity in later chapters. It is important to keep in mind, especially today with the Internet culture, where endless debate and the need to prove someone is "wrong on the Internet" can become a hazard. A snare I struggle with.

**Titus 3:10**
*A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject.*..

As Jesus instructs the Apostles, shake the dust. When we are out soul-winning, going door to door with the gospel, never get into arguments with the unreceptive or the mockers or blasphemers. You simply let them oppose themselves and move on.

Remembering that the foolish despise wisdom is a great way to train yourself to not be trapped in debate, but to say your piece and move on. Their own blood is on their own head. Wash your hands of it.

teachings.title: The wise son and the diligent hand
teachings.summary: Proverbs contrasts the diligent, righteous and wise with the lazy fool; God provides for those who work, and the wise gather the harvest, including winning souls.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 10** begins the more familiar listing of wise sayings, made in the Spirit by Solomon, his proverbs. But the lesson contrasting the righteous listening to instruction, being industrious, refraining from speaking evil and being wise, with the fool who is lazy, full of iniquity and violence, with a froward mouth, continues to be the primary theme carried over from the introduction in chapters 1-9.

Verse 1 contains an eternal truth that any parent could attest to. Establishing early the wisdom to found is accurate and true. A wise son is the pride of a dad, while the foolish son is the heaviness and sorrow of his mother.

From this base, the sayings stack up, precept upon precept, truth on truth. Building a foundation of wisdom that, sadly is lacking in the world today, because most, even many Christians, don't harken to the word of God. They do not fear Him, and so do not have His wisdom to rely on. They do not acknowledge Him in all their ways, and so He isn't there to direct their paths.

There are also proverbs given that have become ingrained in the secular lexicon (even if they don't acknowledge it). Such as the first half of verse 2; Gain made by wicked deeds profit nothing. In other words, crime doesn't pay. But the wise counter to this truth is that the way of the righteous delivers one from death.

We are told the truth of the Lord that He will provide for His own, the righteous won't famish, while He destroys the substance of the wicked. Not a prosperity gospel, but the understanding that when you walk in the Spirit, working in righteousness, the Lord will take care of your basic needs.

**Luke 12:27-31**
*Consider the lilies how they grow: they toil not, they spin not; and yet I say unto you, that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these. If then God so clothe the grass, which is to day in the field, and to morrow is cast into the oven; how much more will he clothe you, O ye of little faith? And seek not ye what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink, neither be ye of doubtful mind. For all these things do the nations of the world seek after: and your Father knoweth that ye have need of these things. But rather seek ye the kingdom of God; and all these things shall be added unto you.*

This is a promise of Christ Jesus Himself, with the caveat that the poor often are that way by being slackers, not diligent in their works.

**2 Thessalonians 3:10**
*For even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if any would not work, neither should he eat.*

God blesses those that prepare, gathering in the summer against the winter is wise. Sleeping through the harvest is a shame. Being forward thinking and considering the end of something, understanding consequences, cause and effect, is wisdom. Shortsighted sin leads to shame.

Of course, the harvest analogy is not just applicable to agrarian cultures, or to earthly financial goals, but also the sharing of the gospel of Christ's Kingdom is frequently likened to the harvest.

**John 4:35**
*Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest.*

Go soul-winning! The workers are few and the harvest is plenty. He that winneth souls is wise.

**Psalm 126:6**
*He that goeth forth and weepeth, bearing precious seed, shall doubtless come again with rejoicing, bringing his sheaves with him.*

But the sluggard who buries his talent of silver, to mix metaphors, he will be ashamed. He will not have sheaves of glory to rejoice in.

Being a just man, fair and merciful, extending grace to others, brings blessings and glory. The Lord will esteem the name of the just but the fool will die unknown, they will fall.

Walk upright, consider what you say. Don't be a prattling fool or a subtle and froward man, or a man of violence and offense, stirring up strifes and hatred. Knowing love covereth all sins.

**1 Peter 4:8**
*And above all things have fervent charity among yourselves: for charity shall cover the multitude of sins.*

teachings.title: Reprove not a scorner; shake off the dust
teachings.summary: As Christ and Paul taught, we do not argue with scorners when giving the gospel but shake off the dust and move on, while instruction to the wise makes them wiser, each man bearing his own guilt.
teachings.text:
Solomon then gives this instruction; *Forsake the foolish, and live.* He says to not reprove a scorner, to not rebuke the wicked. This is echoed in the way Christ gave to His disciples when sending them out to the lost sheep of Israel;

**Mathew 10:14** *And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet*.

As Paul instructs Titus;

**Titus 3:10** *A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject*

These men oppose themselves.

Peter writes that we should not argue with scoffers; *Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing*.

**1 Peter 3:16** *Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.*

When we are out in the hedges and highways, compelling all to come to the wisdom of God, by His gospel, we aren't there to argue. To debate. We are not supposed to waste our time with scoffers and mockers and scorners of the truth. We are supposed to shake the dust and move on.

But, if we give instruction to the wise, they will be wiser. Those seeking the truth will hear us. They will understand that the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.

And by His wisdom, our days are lengthened, our life increased.

It is on every man to bear this. To the wise, for themselves and to life; for the scorner, to themselves unto death.

This is individual soul liberty. We carry our own guilt and are responsible. But by faith we enter into His grace.

teachings.title: Living waters flowing out from Jerusalem
teachings.summary: The river from Ezekiel's temple pictures the Spirit and the gospel flowing out from Jerusalem, with believers as fruitful trees by the river as in Psalm 1 and John 7.
teachings.text:
Here in the penultimate chapter of Ezekiel, continuing with the prophecy of the Temple, we find the prophet brought out with the man guiding him before, who had the measure in his hands, and observing the flowing of water out of the altar and beyond the Temple and the courtyard.

And the further they went, the deeper the water became, from his ankle to his knees, to his loins. Eventually, to a mighty river that could not be passed over, deep enough to swim in.

Returning to the river's brink, the shore along a steep rise, and there he observed the trees on both sides. The angels tells him that the waters themselves that issue out of the Temple will eventually fill the desert, and the seas, healing all they touch, everything *shall live whither the river cometh*.

Living waters emanating from Jerusalem, trees lining their banks.

In **Psalm 1**, the Bible says we who delight in the Lord and His word are like unto trees planted by a river, that brings forth fruit, and the leaves shall not whither.

The prophet Zachariah preaches that in the day of the Lord, among the other things that occur, would be Jesus splitting the mount of Olives in Jerusalem, and in that day *living waters* shall go out from Jerusalem.

In the gospel of John, Jesus says that out of the belly of believers shall flow rivers of living water, and that this was a picture of the Spirit which they that believe on Him should receive.

Later, in the Revelation of Jesus given John, the new Heaven and heavenly Jerusalem has a river, and the tree of life upon it, which gives 12 different fruits every month, and whose leaves were for healing the nations.

The natural application for the initial prophecy given Ezekiel is a restored kingdom, with a river of waters healing the land, trees grown up from its shores, and full of all types of fish in abundance.

But spiritually, this is fulfilled in the ministry of Christ, and the spreading of the Gospel, as living waters, the Spirit, and wherever it went, healing the nations, and believers being as trees bearing fruit, other believers, springing up alongside the brink.

Prophetically, this matches the pattern in the end times shown John, of New Jerusalem.

If you are like the righteous man in **Psalm 1**, the believer in **John 7**, you are a tree bearing fruit, and from you flows the Spirit, living waters, His word.

Notice, the river begins in Jerusalem and gets deeper and deeper the further it travels.

And note too, that there are miry places, salt marshes that shall not be healed.

That the Mt Olive prophecy in Zachariah talks about the split, and a war between Judah.

There are those who will not receive the truth. There were Jews who would not believe, and they killed Christ and persecuted His followers.

teachings.title: The remnant are not chosen but seek Him
teachings.summary: The remnant in Amos 5 is not a Calvinist election of certain men but the promise that whoever seeks the Lord shall live.
teachings.text:
**Amos 5** continues the prophesying against Israel, whose destruction is nigh. There is no salvation for her. God's judgment and righteousness are at hand.

But, as always, there are a remnant of believers still in the land. Illustrating this in verse 3, in each of the decimated cities. A remnant because of the promise of the Lord that those who seek Him shall live.

Note that the number is not set in stone, it is an example. The remnant aren't chosen by God, and it isn't a promise that there will be a tenth spared. As with this entire chapter, it is an encouragement to repent towards God.

Many Dispensationalists put the wrong emphasis of there being a remnant on God to elect one. To be a Calvinist God Who forces certain men to be saved. They sometimes argue that verses like this are a guarantee that God has decided to set some people aside to be saved, rather than a process by which they can be. And so, the emphasis should be on the promise, that those who call on His name shall be saved.

Amos, speaking the word of God warns, seek Him, not Bethel in the Northern Kingdom of Israel where a golden calf was set up by King Jeroboam as a false religion. Not in Gilgal, on the Jordan where idolatrous practices to false gods were held. These vain hopes would come to naught.

Seek the Lord and ye shall live!

Failing that, He promises His wrath will consume them.

And they, specifically the children of Joseph, 'all Ephraim" as the prophets call the Northern Kingdom of Israel, deserve it. They turn right judgment to wormwood, thinking it bitter, rejecting the way of righteousness. They rebuke prophets, hating them that preach God's word. They take advantage of the poor and the weak. They build up their riches by their unrighteousness. They afflict the just, take bribes and turn aside the poor seeking help. They show no mercy and so God's mercy is gone from them.

But the offer stands;

*Seek him that maketh the seven stars and Orion, and turneth the shadow of death into the morning, and maketh the day dark with night: that calleth for the waters of the sea, and poureth them out upon the face of the earth: The Lord is his name: That strengtheneth the spoiled against the strong, so that the spoiled shall come against the fortress.*

Amos preaches against sin and warns of the coming judgment, and the offer of hope in salvation by faith in the Lord. Just as we are called to do today.

teachings.title: Heap coals of fire on his head
teachings.summary: Unlike Jonah, believers must show mercy to enemies, including giving them the bread of life and water of the gospel, remembering the mercy God showed them.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 5:44-45**
*But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you; That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.*

**Romans 9:15-16**
*For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion. So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy.*

**Proverbs 25:21-23**
*If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord shall reward thee. The north wind driveth away rain: so doth an angry countenance a backbiting tongue.*

Perhaps the hardest thing in the Christian life, showing mercy to those who hate us and whom we hate. But if God chooses us to be a blessing to another, it isn't on us to question why. We shouldn't be as Jonah.

And if they are hardened against us, that's on them. Our mercy will be as hot coals upon their head.

**Romans 12:20**
*Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head.*

Note the spiritual application of this. Your enemy hungers and thirsts. For what? Food and water? Or truth and the repentance unto faith in Christ?

Will the coals of fire make them angrier and dug in against you? Or remind them of the Hell that awaits them?

Will you withhold that bread that came down from Heaven? The waters of life that you've drank?

Are there many who don't know their right hand from left?

Only God knows.
