Remember the mercy God showed you, and let that be what guides your spirit. Don't be as Jonah, and let your anger consume you.

teachings.title: Take with you words: Hosea's sinner's prayer
teachings.summary: Hosea's final appeal is a sinner's prayer: by confessing with our mouths we receive the free gift of eternal life, not by idols or our own works, and God heals our backsliding.
teachings.text:
Here, in the final chapter of **Hosea**, the Lord speaks through the prophet to make one final appeal of the gospel, that whosoever believes be saved.

He calls for Israel to repentance towards God, that they have fallen in their sin. (For all have fallen short)

*Take with you words, and turn to the Lord: say unto him, Take away all iniquity, and receive us graciously*, this is a sinner's prayer. (That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth...)

We are offered the free gift of eternal life in Christ, by the promise of a gracious God, Who takes away our sins, by the confession of our mouths. By the calves, the sin offering of our lips. Giving thanks to His name.

False gods shall not save us, nor the works of our hands. Note the double meaning here, both idols and literally the trust in our own works. For the Lord God is Father to the fatherless, in His mercy.

He heals our backsliding, loves us freely. We are no longer appointed to His wrath.

The Lord promises we will be watered as the lilies of the field. Taking root, spreading out like an olive tree. Growing as the vine.

And Ephraim, all Israel, will bring forth His fruit. After their kind.

*Who is wise, and he shall understand these things? prudent, and he shall know them? for the ways of the Lord are right, and the just shall walk in them: but the transgressors shall fall therein.*

He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

teachings.title: Turn again unto the Lord, the remnant
teachings.summary: Hezekiah preached to Israel's remnant that God's wrath could still be turned away, and 2 Chronicles 7:14 is a standing promise, so even in a wicked nation we compel men to return to the Lord.
teachings.text:
*Ye children of Israel, turn again unto the Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, and he will return to the remnant of you, that are escaped out of the hand of the kings of Assyria. And be not ye like your fathers, and like your brethren, which trespassed against the Lord God of their fathers, who therefore gave them up to desolation, as ye see. Now be ye not stiffnecked, as your fathers were, but yield yourselves unto the Lord, and enter into his sanctuary, which he hath sanctified for ever: and serve the Lord your God, that the fierceness of his wrath may turn away from you. For if ye turn again unto the Lord, your brethren and your children shall find compassion before them that lead them captive, so that they shall come again into this land: for the Lord your God is gracious and merciful, and will not turn away his face from you, if ye return unto him.*

Hezekiah is preaching the word of God to the lost sheep of Israel. The Northern Kingdom had been made nearly desolate by the Assyrians. A remnant still remained, and Ephraim and Manasseh were yet to be wiped out. There was still time and hope for them as a nation of people who called themselves after His name. The fierceness of His wrath could still be turned away.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

This is a standing promise to Christians, from a God who cannot lie. God, who is longsuffering and merciful, Who rewards those who diligently seek him. Who runs to meet the prodigals coming home to Him.

Very apt timing, the day before our elections here in the United States. Not that a godly person is on the ballot. Not that our wicked nation deserves healing.

But as bad as the people are, and as unclean, we are to compel them to come. To turn back to the Lord, that the fierceness of His wrath be delayed, that a remnant will hear and believe, and His children will get right and sanctify themselves, so that He may forgive us our sin and heal our land.

teachings.title: Why Christ died in this manner
teachings.summary: Every sacrifice from Adam onward pictured the Lamb slain, and the cross and resurrection had to happen before witnesses so that all nations could hear the gospel and believe without seeing.
teachings.text:
I recently was giving the gospel to someone who said, "I understand God loves us, and that His Son, Jesus was born and died and rose again for us, but I struggle with the question; Why?" Not as in why did God do this, which we know is because He so loved us. But why in this manner?

I think one of the reasons is that man by our nature we know sin requires a sacrifice for atonement.

Of course every animal sacrificed from Adam and Eve and God showing them the way, through righteous Abel, to Noah disembarking from the ark, to Abraham with Melchizedek, to Moses and Arron and the Levitical priests, were pictures given by God of the actual sacrifice to come. The Lamb slain before the foundation of the world. And they who trusted in the Christ to come were saved by that faith. But without some means of understanding, it was difficult for them to form faith. Thus the process laid out in the law.

But for the other nations called, after the crucifixion and resurrection, the one sacrifice made for all time, for all sin, by Jesus' blood, man needed to understand it clearly. And so we place trust in His word. Faith being the evidence of things not seen, which comes from hearing His word. There needed to be witnesses. It had to happen here, in this world that others would believe, sight unseen.

As Jesus says to Thomas, *blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.*

Without the prophets and scriptures promising Christ, the sacrifice of Christ, and without the witnesses to the resurrection testifying of Christ, I think man would not believe God wanted to forgive them. Without the gospel preached, a witness, exactly as it stands:

**1 Corinthians 15:1-8**
*Moreover, brethren, I declare unto you the gospel which I preached unto you, which also ye have received, and wherein ye stand; By which also ye are saved, if ye keep in memory what I preached unto you, unless ye have believed in vain. For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures: And that he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve: After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once; of whom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep. After that, he was seen of James; then of all the apostles. And last of all he was seen of me also, as of one born out of due time.*

teachings.title: Tearing down his father's altar
teachings.summary: Saved believers surrounded by false religion, even family, should stand for the Lord like Gideon, since faithful obedience convinces others more than words.
teachings.text:
Gideon, the son of Joash, from the Abiezrite clan, was of the tribe of Manasseh, living in Ophrah, which is on the promised land side of the Jordan, where the western half tribe of Manasseh resided. The Midianites, on the eastern side of the Jordan south of Edom and Moab. This is how extensive the reach of the Midianites were, as they rated Israel to take as spoil everything they planted. God sent them against Israel for their falling away and worship of Baal.

And to drive home the point of how extensive that abomination was, We see that all of the people living in Ophrah including his own father, worshiped at an altar and a grove dedicated to the Canaanite god.

Gideon was clearly a believer in the Lord, though he questioned why they suffered so. But he knew why, He was surrounded by it. It was punishment for their adultery.

Today many Christians, especially those of us who may have gotten saved from a Bible way to heaven video, or through talking to people online, or by a door-knocker on a missions trip or soul-winning marathon. They believe in the Lord and call upon Jesus name and are saved, yet they are surrounded by people who believe in a false god. It can be very difficult in those situations to stand up for the Lord against the popular opinion of those around us. Including our families. It can be hard to do the right thing.

But we see Gideon instructed to tear down the altar and burn the wood of the grove, and he does so. And when the men come inquiring who did it, Gideon's active faith in service to the Lord. Reveals the dead idol that they had been worshiping, his wayward father leading his defense.

Often that is all it takes to bring other people to the understanding of the Lord. To just stand up and do the next right thing as He is presented it to you. Our faithful obedience can convince people far more than our words. And often the only hindrance to doing something great for the Lord that brings others around to the truth is our own fear.

teachings.title: Every man shall give as he is able
teachings.summary: Blessed by God, believers give back as they are able in two main ways, winning souls and executing right judgment for the fatherless and widow.
teachings.text:
*Every man shall give as he is able, according to the blessing of the Lord thy God which he hath given thee.*

What a concisely phrased explanation of the Christian life, and God's expectations for us. He blessed us, His children. He asks in return that we give to Him as we are able, according to those blessings.

The giving isn't required for the blessing. But the blessing asks for the giving. And we know that there are two main ways the Lord asks us to give unto Him; winning souls and right judgment.

What a day when we are bringing in the sheaves! When the fullness of man has come in, and to the Lord is given the increase.

As the parables of the sower, the wise servant, and others told by Jesus, picturing the Kingdom of God and the fruit that we are called to bring forth, after our kind. The winning of souls through the gospel.

And in judgement, knowing; *Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted.*

It's no coincidence that the reminder of keeping the feasts, bringing the gifts, remembering the blessings given by the Lord to us, is followed immediately by;

*Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates, which the Lord thy God giveth thee, throughout thy tribes: and they shall judge the people with just judgment.*

That we are to be unspotted, blameless in our judgement. Not being a respecter of persons. Not showing favor to one over another, but executing right judgment. Not taking bribes, which would pervert out judgment. That we be just in our ways that we may live.

The two things we are separated unto God's ministry in the Gospel to do, linked forever in the feasts that are Christ's.

teachings.title: Provoke to emulation and save some
teachings.summary: Paul's wish is that by provoking his kinsmen to jealousy he might save some, conditions that dispensationalists twist into will and all.
teachings.text:
So consider this context as we read the next verse;

*Now if the fall of them be the riches of the world, and the diminishing of them the riches of the Gentiles; how much more their fulness?*

Paul says he is speaking to the Gentiles here. Asking them a question as the apostle to them; if the world is made rich in Christ because the unregenerate Jews fell, can you imagine how much more the glory of God would be revealed by their coming to believe?

Recall that Paul's still talking about his own wish, that his brethren after the flesh be saved. He has already concluded that only a remnant are, and that blindness has come on the rest. That only by being part of the election of grace, given to believers, that they can be saved and made heirs in Christ. God is not a respecter of persons. There is no Jew or Greek in Christ.

In that context, we can see Paul's wish for them expressed by the rhetorical question he asks the reader; if their fall was to bring salvation to the world, how much greater would it be if the salvation of the world brought them back?

*If by any means I may provoke to emulation then which are of my flesh, and might save some of them.*

This is the point of the jealousy God hopes to provoke in them. That some might be saved.

If...may...might...some.

Many dispensationalists will twist this series of conditions to mean "will" and "all."

teachings.title: Peace, peace, when there is no peace
teachings.summary: False prophets preach peace, prosperity and a pre-tribulation escape to itching ears, but true preachers warn of judgment and call men to repent and find peace only in Christ.
teachings.text:
**Jeremiah 6:13-15**
*For from the least of them even unto the greatest of them every one is given to covetousness; and from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely. They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace. Were they ashamed when they had committed abomination? nay, they were not at all ashamed, neither could they blush: therefore they shall fall among them that fall: at the time that I visit them they shall be cast down, saith the Lord.*

**1 Thessalonians 5:1-3**
*But of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you. For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night. For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them, as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape.*

False prophets, claiming to speak the words of God, come with soothing words of peace. Peace with God, despite the sins of the people. Peace with the land, despite the blood of innocents. Peace with those who practice Idolatry and wickedness, in ecumenicalism.

They preach prosperity and health to people with itching ears.

**2 Timothy 4:3-4**
*For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears; and they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables.*

Today, many false prophets also claim that believers won't see tribulation, but rather will be spared destruction, raptured before it begins.

But what does Jeremiah say to Hannah? *The prophets that have been before me and before thee of old prophesied both against many countries, and against great kingdoms, of war, and of evil, and of pestilence.*

Prophets who come with the word of God preach destruction and repentance.

And, in like manner, today we have the word of God, and we are called to do the same.

**Jude 1:22-23**
*And of some have compassion, making a difference: and others save with fear, pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh.*

We preach the acceptable year of the Lord. That judgment is coming to every man, and Hell with it. To repent towards God and faith in His Son for deliverance. That man cannot know peace except in Christ. These are the word of God given us in scripture with the command to love one another, to set at liberty from the bonds of the law. To reconcile man with God before it's too late.

**Matthew 11:28-30**
*Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.*

teachings.title: We have no excuse
teachings.summary: Since we do not face death for preaching as the prophets did, we have no excuse not to serve, and should rejoice in tribulation.
teachings.text:
Be thankful for living when we do, in times where we aren't directly threatened with stocks, stripes or death for the preaching of the cross. We have no excuse.

We live in a time and place where, while we may see tribulation, where we may have the god of this world come against us if we strive for the Gospel, doing our Father's will. Winning souls. Edifying the brethren. We won't face death the way the prophets did. Praise God.

And so we have no excuse.

In fact, if you have done anything for the Lord, you may have already felt the attacks of Satan and his children on you. And yet, if you rejoice in the temptations and praise God for the tribulation that worketh patience in you, you will be delivered.

We have no excuse.

And if the times become more hostile, and persecution for the faith more common, still rejoice.

**Matthew 10:28**
*And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell*.

We will still have no excuse.

teachings.title: Bloom where the Lord has planted you
teachings.summary: Like Jeremiah, who longed to flee to the wilderness but was sent to preach at the temple gates, Christians are not to retreat to compounds but to be a light where people are, enduring tribulation with hope because Christ has overcome the world.
teachings.text:
*Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them! for they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men.*

**Jeremiah 9** continues his prophesying, the hard preaching of the words of God against the children of Israel that remain in Judea.

And in it, the lamentation to seek to flee from Jerusalem and the wickedness of this generation, and go to the wilderness, to live off grid, and be away from the evil people, uncircumcised in the heart.

But God calls upon Jeremiah to preach in the city, by the gates of the Temple. To tell them of the pending destruction their forsaking Him has brought up on them.

This same impulse is given to Christians today. To flee the world, to get to a redoubt in the wilderness. To be far from the fallen society that, like just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked.

But, like the prophets, and like Christ Himself, we go to Jerusalem. We are called to go to the population centers and preach the acceptable year of the Lord. To seek that which is lost. To be a light in that darkness.

We can't be a light to others if we are hidden in the woods.

And so we are in the world, not of it.

Rather than coveting a RETVRN to a past we never knew, or a rustic compound in the hills, we are supposed to bloom where the good Lord has planted us. To be a blessing to those around us. To *be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ*.

Not to flee persecution, and the tribulations that come to every believer, living for the Lord. To *glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.*

**James 1:12**
*Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.*

**Romans 8:18**
*For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.*

**James 1:2-4**
*My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.*

We who believe on Christ have already overcome this fallen world. Because He has overcome death and Hell for us. We shouldn't be black pilled. We may wail with lamentations for our people to repent, but standfast in the faith that has saved us.

**John 16:33**
*These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.*

teachings.title: What must I do to be saved
teachings.summary: Answering a seeker with repent of your sins instead of believe on the Lord Jesus Christ only leads to confusion, discouragement and perdition.
teachings.text:
And imagine being an unsaved but seeking person, desperate to know what they must do to be saved, like the Philipian jailer, and you ask "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?"

And the answer isn't "Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ," but instead is "well, you have to repent of your sins."

"What does that mean? Like stop sinning? What if I can't? Which sins? The really bad ones? What if I don't realize it's a sin? What if I slip up?"

"Well, try to avoid sin. You have to want to avoid sin."

"How? I can't be saved if I don't try to avoid sin? I already am trying not to drink/smoke/watch porn. Is that good enough? How will I know if it's good enough? If I'm good enough?"

"Well then make Jesus your boss. Make him the Lord of your life."

"Isn't He already? What does that even mean? Do I have to sell everything and follow Him like the young rich man?"

Etc...

It is not a Gospel presentation. It's an invitation to confusion, discouragement and perdition.

teachings.title: Abortion: passing children through the fire
teachings.summary: Abortion is today's child sacrifice to Molech and Mammon, and the women burdened by it should be reached with the gospel before their hearts are hardened.
teachings.text:
*And thou shalt not let any of thy seed pass through the fire to Molech, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy God: I am the Lord*.

Sacrifice of children to false gods was a common practice in every age and nation. We know that today, it is done through abortion. In Canaan, they sacrificed to Moloch. Today, it is often Mammon. It is horribly wicked. The bloody sacrifices to devils of their own children leads many to reprobation.

Women today have been pressured with unrelenting propaganda and social and economic incentives to use abortifacients as "birth control" and infanticide, while men have abandoned their proper role as a husband and father. Many, especially the women, carry this burden of sin and pain and are brokenhearted from it. It is important to try and reach them with the Gospel before they harden their hearts to sear their conscience.

teachings.title: Condescend to men of low estate
teachings.summary: Do not think yourself above the poor and broken, who are often most receptive to the gospel, remembering Christ humbled Himself for us.
teachings.text:
This is also speaking of not being a respecter of persons in a material sense. Understand that the more lowly and sinful and broken a person is, there's a strong likelihood that they will be receptive to the Gospel. Don't think better of yourself because someone is poor, uneducated, simple, not of your class or status. They aren't beneath you. Be their servants, ministering the Gospel in love.

Jesus Christ who is the holy Son of God, was made flesh, subject to the corruption of the world, made sin for our sakes, suffering the humiliation of the cross, pain and death, the fires of Hell, all for our benefit, while we were yet sinners.

Keep that in mind.

teachings.title: Blessed is he not offended in me
teachings.summary: John's doubt was answered by the works Jesus did, showing it is fine to seek confirmation of our hope but we must believe the report and not be ashamed of the gospel.
teachings.text:
And so this act, and others like it, begin to be spread throughout the land. All of Judea hears the rumors of Christ; *That a great prophet is risen up among us; and, That God hath visited his people.*

And hearing this word go out, many come to faith. Yet others find their faith shaken and tested.

John the Baptist, in prison for his preaching of repentance at the coming of Christ, hearing these things. In bonds, separated from the outside world, probably feeling occasional despair. Doubt.

And so hearing of these signs and wonders, John seeks to know; is Jesus the Christ as he believed? Is it his faith confirmed? Is it too good to be true? And so, he sends disciples to ask Jesus, directly. *Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?*

The Bible doesn't give us an immediate answer from Jesus. He doesn't tell them, He shows. That very hour Jesus heals infirmities and casts out spirits. Restoring sight to the blind.

Then Jesus answered. He says tell John what you have seen. Jesus doesn't argue His divinity or that He is the Christ. He lets His actions justify Him before man, that they may know and believe, and bring this good news to John. *How that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached.*

His mission statement. The prophecy of Isaiah made real.

**James 2:22**
*Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?*

We are saved by faith alone. Justified before God in Christ. Not of our dead works. In much the same way, John's faith in Jesus being the Christ that he hoped for, that he believed in, is made perfect by the work Jesus did. By the witness and testimony of what those disciples had seen. His doubt assuaged, I am sure.

And Jesus adds; *And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.*

Offended in the Gospels means shaken of faith. Turned aside from the correct path by shame or doubt or the behavior of another. By false teachings. And here Jesus is saying that we who aren't shaken, who are not ashamed of the Gospel, who aren't troubled by the truth of who Christ is and what He has done for us, are blessed. The antihisis of **Mark 8:38**: 

*Whosoever therefore shall be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation; of him also shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he cometh in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.*

It is ok to have doubts. To seek a confirmation for the hope we have, but at the end of the day we are to believe the report. To trust God and His promises. To believe the witness of others, and to hear His word and have faith, unashamed.

*For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth.*..

teachings.title: The Wisdom of God Against the Vexation of the World
teachings.summary: The wisdom of this world brings despair, but the foolishness of the gospel gives rest, wisdom and joy to all who come to Christ.
teachings.text:
The despondency of the natural man is manifest in how we react to the wisdom of this world. To the toil and drudgery that is a life without meaning. The same folly that our fathers endured and that our children will face. The wickedness and sin throughout the world. Evil called good and good, evil. The weakness of others and the burdens they become on our shoulders. A yoke that leads to bitterness, resentment, wrath, covetousness and a host of other sins and the vices that we take up to fill the time and dull the pain. Even a "good man" has their patience stretched thin and feels the despair more acutely it seems.

But then there's the wisdom of God, which makes the weak strong and brings forth the truth of the things the world hates to bring to nought that which they love.

And the foolishness of the Gospel is the power unto salvation. That God became man, dwelled among us, sinless, to do the will of God unto death that we who deserve Hell are made righteous in His blood. And the resurrection of Christ giving us the hope of our faith, that we have eternal life through the grace and mercy of God the Father.

And by that faith, we are given wisdom and knowledge and strength. The power of sanctification and redemption in the day of judgment that all men are appointed to.

And so, we rejoice. We rejoice in tribulation knowing we have triumphed. We give glory to God in suffering and in blessings. We patiently wait for His return, while being a light to those still in darkness.

If you're not 100% certain, today, right now, that if you died today you would go to Heaven. If you're scared and alone and feel hopeless. If you're carrying guilt and trauma and regrets that are tearing you up inside. If you're seeking answers and wisdom, but only finding despair and vexation. If you're struggling to find an identity, a place in a world that makes no sense to you at times. If you have been laboring to be righteous, to cleanse your sins by your own works, and frustrated with how fruitless it is to obtain righteousness on your own, please consider this presentation of the Bible way to Heaven. You don't have to carry the burden. Jesus already has done it for you.

*Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.*

teachings.title: Hell Is Real, Eternal Torment
teachings.summary: Hell is a real place of eternal torment in the presence of the Lamb, not the grave, annihilation or Satan's kingdom, so some must be saved with fear.
teachings.text:
**Revelation 14**
*8 And there followed another angel, saying, Babylon is fallen, is fallen, that great city, because she made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication.*

*9 And the third angel followed them, saying with a loud voice, If any man worship the beast and his image, and receive his mark in his forehead, or in his hand,*

*10 The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb:*

*11 And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: and they have no rest day nor night, who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name.*

Continuing chapter 14, we see angels proclaiming first the Gospel, then in verse 8, hailing the destruction of Babylon. This will be dealt with in somewhat greater detail in chapter 17.

The third angel heralds the damnation of those who worship the beast and take his mark, their place in wrath and Hell assured. And important doctrine is found in these verses; that Hell is real, eternal, and that the torment of the damned takes place in the presence of the Lamb, Christ Jesus.

There are false doctrines that make many claims regarding Hell, or what happens in death to those unregenerate souls who don't accept the free gift of salvation. Satan and his children have tried to cast doubt on Hells existence, claiming it is simply the grave, "Sheol." Barring that, they will say it's not eternal, that the soul is consumed and annihilation is swift.

Others claim that Hell is just a dark empty void, or being cut off from the presence of God, which they claim is worse than simply being tormented by fire.

And of course there are those who claim Satan himself is ruler of Hell and his demons are tormenting spirits used against the damned, pitchforks and devils.

But the Bible tells us these are heretical and silly views, and none more clearly than here in Revelation.

The souls are condemned to be bound in Hell with the Devil. Hell was created especially for Satan and his fallen angels, according to Jesus in **Matthew 25:41** "*Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels.*"

God's wrath is a fire that pours out from Him, and the damned are tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels and Christ, the smoke of their torment rises up for eternity, and they have no rest day or night from this torment.

This is why we are called to be servants of the Lord who saved us. To be a light unto the world and give testimony to the Gospel. Saving some with kindness and charity, magnifying the grace God has extended on we who are saved, that it may guide those seeking the light to the truth. But some require more than that. They require fear. Fear of judgment and the punishment, the wages of their sin. The Bible says those we should *save with fear, pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh.*

teachings.title: A crown of righteousness for all who love His appearing
teachings.summary: Paul charges Timothy to preach the word in season and out, and finishes his course assured of the crown of righteousness that all who love Christ's appearing will receive when works are tried.
teachings.text:
I'm not crying you are crying.

Paul, having come close to the end of his life, having written to Timothy, his son in Christ whom he led to salvation, grew in the faith, laid hands on for the gifts of the Holy Ghost and sent out into Asia Minor to evangelize and spread the gospel, planting churches, charging his protege with teaching the fundamentallist doctrines of God, reaches his summation. A poignant and inspiring end.

Paul charges Timothy on God, in the name of Jesus, who will judge the quick and the dead, the living and the damned at His coming, to please be faithful to the doctrines he's left him.

*Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all long suffering and doctrine.*

The word of God must be preached, we must be ready with scripture, when it's popular and when it isn't, especially. For we must be, as Timothy, ready to use all scripture to teach, strengthen and correct those seeking truth. To whom God has called to us in the Holy Spirit.

And this cause is great because, as Paul warns, people will wax cold to the truth, and turn towards fables and false doctrines that satisfy their itching ears, that justify and rationalize their sin, rather than lead them to the truth. So, as a stalwart in the faith, armed with the word, we, like Timothy must endure, for the sake of the elect that they may know the grace of God and His salvation.

And we understand Paul's plea, that he facing uncertainty, and his impending death in this life, seeks to ensure the tradition of the Gospel lives on in his "son."

*For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:*

*Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.*

This is the crown we should all strive for, the reward of those who work towards His coming.

The Bible says; *Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth. and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven.*

For Jesus will judge the quick, as well as the dead. We who believe and are given the gift of eternal life will see our works judged;

*Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is.*  *If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.*

As Paul says, *Every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible.*

And in Paul's striving for mastery, his running a good race, having fought the good fight, he knows with certainty as his end approaches, with that blessed assurance of the Spirit testifying within him, by the word that he has his hope in, that he will be rewarded by God as promised. For God is not slack regarding His promises. He is faithful in all things. Amen

teachings.title: To day if ye will hear his voice
teachings.summary: God's call and light last only for a time, as the door of the ark was shut, so the unbelieving must repent and believe on Christ today.
teachings.text:
The meat of the word, giving us instruction on how we should carry ourselves as saved Christians, to be a good witness, to live faith to faith, growing in the spirit, studying to be approved unto God, understanding the liberty we have in Christ, what the implications are for those of us possessing eternal life, what to expect at Jesus' coming, God's plan and promise, His justice and wrath...all this is impossible to understand without first understanding salvation in Christ. Without which you cannot receive even the milk of the word, as born again babes.

The light of the Lord shines on us for a brief time, the Spirit convicts and draws the unbelieving to the light for a limited time, and then if a person remains unreceptive, is hid away. God gives every opportunity to you to repent and believe on Jesus Christ for salvation, but it isn't limitless.

*To day if ye will hear his voice,*
*Harden not your heart...behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation...Seek ye the Lord while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near!*

Just as God was longsuffering to the unbelieving as Noah built his ark, and then shut the door, too late to be saved, so to is His offer of grace.

*While ye have light, believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light. These things spake Jesus, and departed, and did hide himself from them.*

If you have not believed on Jesus Christ as the ONLY means of forgiveness and righteousness, if you have not accepted God's free gift of salvation, if you have been being called to the wedding feast, but have made excuse not to accept, or are trying to work your way in, repent.

Tomorrow is not promised. You are being called today. Don't wait until it is too late. Don't harden your heart.

teachings.title: Souls won, our crown of rejoicing
teachings.summary: Every soul we help bring to Christ is our joy and crown at His coming, the gold that remains when our works are tried by fire.
teachings.text:
Wrapping up the chapter, Paul laments having spent little time with them, wishing it could have been more and, regretting that Satan had hindered his plans to return to them, assures that they will be together at Christ's return, and as souls won, be Paul and Silas' glory and joy. A crown of rejoicing, given as reward.

Every soul we help bring towards Christ and reconciliation with God through the blood of the lamb, whether it be a seed sown, watered or harvested, is our glory and joy in Christ's coming. Our reward at His judgment of our works. A crown given us, a precious stone, after the wood, hay and stubble are burned away.

**1 Corinthians 3:9-15**
*For we are labourers together with God: ye are God's husbandry, ye are God's building. According to the grace of God which is given unto me, as a wise masterbuilder, I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon. For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.*

*Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is.*

*If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.*

teachings.title: An example of the believers
teachings.summary: When loved ones are perishing, believers should stay steadfast and peaceful as an example, since no one will believe our hope if we are as fearful as everyone else.
teachings.text:
A common lament of the believer is that their friends and family are perishing, damned without faith. The worry and stress of having that knowledge and their inability to convince them of the truth leaves many feeling impotent and frustrated. But this is all the more reason to remain steadfast. To magnify God's love for us, reflecting it to those we care about. To be the rock that they can turn to when they are troubled, and maybe coming to see the truth of the word though our example. The reason for our hope. To be *an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.*

Why would someone believe someone telling them of the peace that passes all understanding found in Christ when we are as miserable and fearful as everyone else?

teachings.title: Lovest thou me? Feed my sheep
teachings.summary: Like Peter going back to fishing, saved believers drift into the world, but Christ restores them to feed His sheep and win souls, and each should follow Him without comparing himself to others.
teachings.text:
The final chapter in the Gospel of John is a kind of postscript to John's account of his time with Jesus during His earthly ministry and after His resurrection, a personal recounting of one of the appearances of the risen Christ, and a redemption arc for the apostle Peter.

Now, during this time, after having been shown their faith wasn't in vain, that Jesus is the Christ and the Son of God, but prior to His final ascension on Pentecost, it seems that some of the disciples, Simon Peter chief among them, grew restless absent their Lord. Jesus appeared unto them but wasn't the ever present fixture leading them He had been for the past 3 years. Yes they were saved, yes they knew they had salvation, and yes they knew God's word was true, and yet when left to their own devices, Peter and the others returned to their old ways. Gone a fishing.

This is something many if not most newer Christians experience, or even young Christians brought up in the faith. The rush of joy and the zeal for our Lord gives way to our habits and old life, or, without direction fades to mundane tasks of this world instead of living for the God who bought them.

As David, a man after God's own heart wrote: *Restore unto me the joy of Thy salvation; and uphold me with Thy free spirit.* It happens to the best of us. That level of zeal is difficult to maintain at times.

Peter, one of the greatest Christians, who did so much for the Lord experienced this, and his leadership role lead him to take others along with him, back to the everyday life they'd left behind following Jesus. Not backslidden in sin necessarily, but back to the grind of the world. Carnal but not sinful. More aimless than lost. And here Jesus intervenes.

After an unsuccessful night of fishing, Jesus appears on the shore and in a familiar manner to earlier stories in the Gospels, He directs them to cast their empty nets another way, and they are amazed at the fill of the catch.

I think this is both real and a picture of the ministry to come in the great commission and the disciples being "fishers of men." That where there's sparsity of "fish" among the Jews, Jesus is showing them that casting a wider net out in a different direction, to the Gentiles, that the nets will be overflowing and yet not burst. As many fish as they can haul in.

Jesus dines with Peter, John, Thomas and the others, feeding them bread and fish He provides, over the fire He built. A picture of things.

The risen Christ is a bodily resurrection, Jesus eats. He's not a ghost or spirit, but risen in the flesh.

After they eat, Jesus tempts Peter three times with the question "*Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me?"* And Peter, three times, swears that he does, and that Jesus knows that he does. Just as Peter had denied Jesus thrice before the cock crowed just weeks earlier, Jesus has given him a chance to redeem himself, and direction for his life if he truly loved Jesus. "Feed my sheep."

This is the direction given to all saved believers, to be part of that royal priesthood. To be His disciples. To share the Gospel and win the souls of those lost sheep. To be fishers of men. It's a personal and touching form of the great commission.

Jesus indicates to Peter where his discipleship shall lead, and John as narrator explains to the reader that it's to a martyrs death that glorified God if Peter follows Him. If he feeds His sheep.

With that understanding, Jesus says "Follow me," and Peter does, with John coming along.

Here we see another instance of Peters personality, why Jesus named him a stone. Peter, processing the death he should die for his following Jesus and feeding His sheep turns and points to John and says basically, "what about him?" It's classic Simon Peter.

Jesus' reply, "*If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me."* is a gentle rebuke and reminder that we aren't to worry so much about how other saved Christians walk their Christian life, but rather concentrate on our own. If one does nothing, that's not excuse for ourselves.

teachings.title: Do we live so our loved ones would follow
teachings.summary: With family and friends rejecting the gospel, believers should ask whether their fearless, grateful, Bible-reading, gospel-preaching lives would draw others to Christ.
teachings.text:
This is a powerful and sobering thought. Knowing your dad or mom, sister or brother, son or daughter, reject the Gospel and on the road to reprobation, or who are trapped in their zeal without knowledge, working their way to Hell by not obeying the Gospel.

We know God is perfectly just. We know in His love we are saved, undeserved, entirely by grace, because we have believed the report. But do we live in a way that these people who we care about can emulate? Would they want to? What advantage do they see in accepting salvation, in how you live?

Are you fearful? Do you stress from the news of the world, the fake and gay theater the beast system presents to keep the cattle in pens for slaughter?

Do you live in gratitude and prayer to God in Jesus name?

Do you read your Bible and go to church? Do you boldly proclaim the Gospel to every creature, giving a ready and meek answer to the lively hope you have in Christ?
